Lesson No. 189 — At a Glance

The Islamic personality was being formed on the battlefield of trials and incidents. After the rising of each new day and after each new incident, this personality became clearer, and its features emerged more distinctly. The Muslim community (jama'at muslimah) was being shaped from individuals who possessed distinctive abilities, held distinctive values of life, and whose way and manner were entirely different from all other societies.

Against this community, some event would occur from time to time, and these events became a great trial (fitnah) for the community. This trial operated in the way that the "trial" (fitnah) of gold operates. Through this trial, the genuine essence and the dross were separated. The reality of people and their true nature came to the surface. The scum was removed and pure gold was set apart. In this way, values in which there was adulteration were eliminated from the Islamic society.

In these trials, the Qur'an would be revealed, or commentary would be given on events and incidents after they occurred. In this commentary, the events were related, shed light upon, and their rises and falls were explained. Thus the position of each party became evident. The conscience, understanding, intention and resolve were reformed, and guidance was given in the light of these events, so that people would clearly understand that guidance and be deeply influenced by it, and correct themselves. In this way, the training of the Islamic community continued every day, and after every incident it received guidance, and the personality of this community was shaped according to the goals of the Islamic system of life, and it received impressions from these commentaries.

It did not happen that all the rulings and guidance were revealed in one go and placed before the Muslims, and then it was said: "Go and act upon them." Rather, these guidance and laws were revealed after events: trials came, tests came, and incidents occurred, and revelation came from that side, because Allah, the Bountiful Creator, knew that human morals can be moulded into a new form and firmly established only through gradualness. The contours of human morality can be corrected only through trials and incidents, that is, in the form of experiential events. Because as a result of practical experience, a matter penetrates to the depths of hearts, and the nerves also begin to move in accordance with it. These nerves then display a fresh response, in the same way that a human being's natural response occurs in the field of battle or in events and incidents. In such events, when the Qur'an was revealed, it would make clear what the event was, what factors lay behind it, and what the Islamic response of a Muslim should be. In this way the Islamic personality would emerge from the furnace of trials clean and refined; the heat of trial would remove every kind of dross from its moral body, and then Islam could mould these personalities into whatever form it wished.

It was a remarkable era that the Muslims passed under the leadership of the Prophet (ﷺ). In it, the heavens and the earth seemed joined. There was a direct connection between the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth. Through all events and all discussions, guidance came from the heavens. Every Muslim lived night and day in the awareness that Allah was watching and hearing. Lest any guidance or commentary should come down, lest any word, any action, or even any intention of his should become the cause of revelation, lest it become manifest to the people, lest a commentary should come from the Messenger of Allah concerning him. It was as though every Muslim felt that he was directly connected with the Lord, the Exalted. If he faced some matter or some difficulty, he would wait for some ruling, some guidance, some decision to come down from the heavens, and that Allah Himself would tell him: "O so-and-so, you said this, you said that, you thought thus; you displayed this and concealed that; do this, do not do that, and do not adopt such conduct." It was a remarkable era, in which a specific command of Allah would arrive concerning a specific person, and this command would be for him and also for all the inhabitants of the earth, for every particle of the earth, indeed for the whole earth.

The truth is that it was a remarkable era. When a person today reflects upon it, recounts its events and incidents, reads and teaches them, he can well form a picture in his mind and see a scene of how extraordinary that era was. But Allah, the Exalted, did not train the Muslims only through awareness, by making their personalities firm; rather, they were made to pass through practical experiences. They were subjected to trials in which they suffered losses, yet gained great benefits, and all these matters were carried out in accordance with Allah's profound wisdoms, because Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware, and He knows well His creation.

What was this wisdom? We ought to reflect upon it at some length, so that we may come to know it, and then ponder over it. And then we should reflect upon the events of life and its trials in its light.

In this lesson, an explanation is given of a great event that confronted the Islamic movement, and in the history of Islam this event was: a great trial for the community of Muslims, and this period was a very hard time for the Ummah. The movement was passing through a very difficult phase, namely the era of the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwah al-Ahzab). This battle took place in the fourth or fifth year after the Hijrah. It was a very great trial for this newly rising movement. All the values and all the principles of the Islamic movement were at stake. By reflecting upon these verses, and from the presentation of the events of the Battle of the Confederates, from its style of expression, from commentary on certain events, from the conduct of certain people, from the thinking of certain individuals, from the apprehensions of certain people, and then from the values that came to light in that battle, it becomes well known how skilfully Allah, through the Qur'an, was training the Ummah.

How the Qur'an comments upon an important event such as the Battle of the Confederates, and in what manner it gives guidance to the Ummah. Before the explanation of the Qur'anic texts, we wish that the complete details of this event be related in some brevity from the books of Seerah, so that we may be able to undertake a comparative study, seeing how human beings relate events and how commentary from Allah is given.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related, with his chain of narration, from a group [of narrators]... In the account of the Battle of the Trench, it is as follows: some Jews, among whom were Sallam ibn Abi'l-Huqayq al-Nadri, Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, Kinanah ibn Abi'l-Huqayq al-Nadri, Hawdhah ibn Qays al-Wa'ili and Abu Ammar al-Wa'ili, and along with them some people from Banu Nadir and some people from Banu Wa'il, were the ones who gathered armies against the Messenger of Allah. These were the first to leave their homes, met the Quraysh, and invited them to wage war against the Messenger of Allah, and they said that they would support them until they uprooted him from his foundation. The Quraysh said: "O community of Jews, you are the people of the first Book, and you know what the dispute is between us and Muhammad (ﷺ). Tell us whether his religion is better or ours." They said: "Your religion is truer than his, and you are more rightly guided than he." These are the ones concerning whom these verses were revealed:

"Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in idols (jibt) and false deities (taghut), and they say of those who disbelieve that they are better guided in the way than those who believe." (4:51) — up to the verses:

"Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom. Among them were some who believed in it and some who turned away from it, and sufficient for those who turn away is the blazing Fire." (4:54–55)

When they gave this verdict to the Quraysh, they were very pleased and became excited, and they consented to fight against the Messenger of Allah. These people then left the Quraysh and went to Ghatafan, who are of the lineage of Qays Ghaylan. They invited them also to fight against Muhammad (ﷺ). They told them that they themselves would support them, and that the Quraysh would also support them; therefore, you should hold a meeting with the Quraysh. Accordingly, the army of the Quraysh set out under the leadership of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Ghatafan with their chief Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Fazari, Harith ibn Awf with Banu Murrah, and Mas'ar ibn Umayyah with his appointed Banu Ashja'.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received reports of this military expedition, he began digging a trench around Madinah. In digging the trench, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also worked, and the Muslims also worked. He laboured diligently, and the Muslims too laboured with great diligence. In this task, in comparison with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, some hypocrites (munafiqin) showed extreme sluggishness. They would engage in very minor tasks and then slip away without the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They would go to their homes, and the Messenger of Allah would not even know. And the practice of the Muslims was that if someone had some necessary matter, he would take permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and leave, and having completed the task he would quickly return, and would work with the utmost zeal and eagerness. Concerning such people this verse was revealed:

"The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter requiring collective effort, they do not leave without his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will, and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." (24:62) Thereafter Allah spoke concerning those who slipped away without permission and shirked work:

"Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of one another. Allah already knows those among you who slip away under cover [of others]. Let those who oppose the Messenger's order beware lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment strike them." (24:63)

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished with the trench, the Quraysh arrived with a great army of Abyssinians, Kinanah and Tihamah, having come from Hara. They camped at Majma' al-Asyal near Darmah, and Ghatafan and their allied tribes camped at Dhanab Naqmi near Uhud. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims numbered three thousand. The back of the Islamic army was towards Mount Sal'. This army halted here, and between the confederate army and the Muslim army there was the trench. He ordered the children and women to take refuge in fortresses.

The enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, met Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi. This was the man who had made a covenant on behalf of Banu Qurayzah; he had given the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) assurance on behalf of his people, and a pact of peace had been made with him by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Huyayy kept clinging to Ka'b ibn Asad and kept inciting him against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He kept making repeated visits to deceive him, until he even obtained from him a promise that if the Quraysh and Ghatafan returned and did not attack Muhammad, he would remain with them in their fortress, so that the same fate that befell them would not befall him. On the strength of these assurances, Ka'b ibn Asad broke the covenant he had made with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and declared his disavowal of the agreement between himself and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Upon this, the difficulties of the Muslims increased, and fear and terror spread. Now the enemy attacked from above and also from below. The Muslims began to entertain all kinds of thoughts in their hearts. The hypocrisy of some hypocrites also began to show. A man, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, of the clan of Banu Amr ibn Awf, was heard saying: "Muhammad (ﷺ) used to make promises to us that we would devour the treasures of Caesar and Chosroes, and today the condition of us is that none of us can go out to relieve himself in safety." And a man of the clan of Banu Haritha, Aws ibn Qayzi, said: "O Messenger, our homes are unprotected," and he said this before his people, and [requested]: "If you give us permission, let us go back to our homes, for our homes are outside Madinah."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also held firm, and the polytheists remained encamped for about a month. The fighting was confined to arrows and the siege. When the people's difficulties increased, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a delegation to Uyayna ibn Hisn and Harith ibn Awf. These two were the leaders of Ghatafan. He offered them that we would give one-third of the dates of Madinah on condition that you return with your men. Peace negotiations took place, and a draft of an agreement was also prepared. The witnessing and signatures had not yet been done when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to sign. He then called Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, chief of the Aws, and Sa'd ibn Ubadah, chief of the Khazraj, and mentioned the agreement to them in their presence and sought their counsel. They said: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), if you like this agreement, it is your choice; sign it. Or if it is a command of Allah, then it is to be obeyed wholeheartedly. And if you wish to do this for our benefit, then tell us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I wish to do this only for your sake. I am doing it only because all of the Arabs are shooting arrows at you from a single bow and have fallen upon you from every side, so I thought that I should reduce their strength somewhat. Upon this, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: We and they were all upon shirk, worshipping idols. They neither worshipped Allah nor recognized Allah. They could not take from us even a single date unless they bought it or we gave it to them as hospitality. Now that Allah has honoured us through Islam, guided us, and given us dignity through you, shall we now give them our hearts? We have no need of this concession. Between us and them the sword will decide. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Do as you wish. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh took the draft and erased whatever had been written in it, and said: Let them do whatever they want against us.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims remained in a state of extreme fear and severity, because the enemy had surrounded them from every side and its strength was great. The Jews had made an agreement with them that they would give the dates of Khaybar if they helped them on this occasion (Tabrizi). Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) says that I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in many difficult and fearful places: the battle of Muraisi', Khaybar, Hudaybiyyah, the conquest of Makkah, and Hunayn. In none of these places did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feel fatigue, nor was he more fearful than in the trench, where the fatigue and fear were the greatest. The Banu Qurayzah were near the women and children. There was a guard in Madinah throughout the night. We Muslims kept hearing the takbir until morning, until Allah Himself turned them back.
An important incident occurred: a man, Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud ibn Amir Ghatafani, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I have become a Muslim, but my people do not know of my Islam. Assign me whatever service you wish, and I can perform it now. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are the only one among us, so restrain the people from fighting against us in whatever way you can, for war is a kind of deception." He carried out an action because of which trust ended between these confederates and the Banu Qurayzah. Its details are fully present in the books of Sirah. Allah also created discord within the confederates and sent such a storm of wind and rain that on a severely cold winter night their tents were uprooted, their cooking pots were overturned, and their hearths were extinguished. When news of their disagreements reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and their unity had broken, he sent Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman to find out the situation of that last night.
Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Zayd ibn Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrated to me: A man from Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "Abu Abdullah! You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and kept his company." He said: "Yes, nephew, I saw and kept his company." He asked: "Then what did you used to do?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive very hard." That man said: "By Allah, if we had found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we would never have let him walk on the earth, and we would have carried him upon our necks." Upon this Hudhayfah said: "Nephew, we took part in the Battle of the Trench with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It happened that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a part of the night and then turned to us and said: 'Who will stand up and go and find out what these people are doing, and then come back? For this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set the condition of return. I will ask Allah that he be my companion in Paradise.'" The fear was so severe that no one stood up. The hunger was so great that no one had the strength, and the cold was also severe. When no one stood up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called my name, I had no other choice. He said: "Hudhayfah, go, enter among those people, see what they are doing, and do not say anything until you come back to us." Hudhayfah says: I went and entered into the army. The storm and the hosts of Allah were doing to them what they were doing. The cooking pots could not stay in their place, and the fire could not be lit. Abu Sufyan stood up and ordered that each person should check the one sitting next to him. I had already asked the person sitting next to me, "Who are you?" He told me, "So-and-so, son of so-and-so." After that Abu Sufyan said: "O people of Quraysh, we cannot stay here any longer. Horses and camels have perished. The Banu Qurayzah have broken their promise to us, and we have received from them an answer we dislike. The storm is as severe as you see. The cooking pots do not stay in place, the fire does not burn, and the tents have been uprooted. So let each of you act. I am leaving now." Saying this, he stood up, took his camel, and it stood on three legs, and he untied its rope while standing. "Had the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not commanded me not to say anything until I came back to him, I would have finished off Abu Sufyan with a single arrow." Hudhayfah says that when I returned, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing and praying in a long, patterned cloak, which belonged to one of his wives. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw me, he drew me in under his feet into the cloak and threw a part of the cloak over me. Then he bowed and prostrated, and I remained wrapped in the cloak. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, I informed him of everything in full. Now, when the Ghatafan heard that Quraysh had done this, they also returned to their territories.
These verses of the Qur'an do not mention the names of individuals. Rather, examples of people are given, and the Qur'an has also left out the detailed particulars and minutiae of the events. The Qur'an records here those values, those characters, and those patterns of conduct which are exemplary and everlasting: characters that are not specific to any event, not specific to any person, and that do not vanish when circumstances pass away. The Qur'an has recorded here those characters and values which are a lesson of warning for future generations and are the desired standard for every group. The Qur'an links all events and incidents to the planning and decree of Allah, and tells how the hand of power supported the Muslims at each stage; at every stage of this battle the divine plan did its work, and the Qur'an presented commentary on each stage.

The Qur'an related this story to those who were present in it, who were its characters. But the Qur'an also lays open before them the causes of which they were unaware, and the aspects of those events and incidents which were hidden from their sight, although they were characters in this story. The Qur'an also opens before them the ups and downs of the human self, and tells the inclinations of people's consciences and what kinds of doubts had arisen in the hearts of people.

Apart from these matters, the beauty of expression, the majesty and grandeur of the speech, the force and warmth of its argument, the humorous manner about the hypocrites, the writhing of their hypocrisy, and the courage and faith of the Muslims, their patience and complete reliance on Allah, in short, all these matters the Qur'an records with great beauty. These Qur'anic texts actually move every reader to action. They do not move only those people who fought these battles, in which they had a fundamental role, and who saw everything; rather, they are inspiring in all subsequent eras and societies as well, whenever the Islamic movement faces circumstances like those that those people faced, even though a long time has passed. If such circumstances arise even in the most modern and diverse societies, these texts keep a believer active in exactly the same way as they kept Muslims active in the early generations.

Only a person who faces the same circumstances that the Muslims of that time faced in the Battle of the Confederates can rightly understand these texts. When such circumstances exist, then springs of guidance flow from these verses, and the hearts of those working for Islam open to their meanings. Now the words and lines of the Qur'an become strength and weapons, and the worker plunges into exactly such battles. Then these verses produce living, awakened, progressive people, and these people rise up carrying a real movement. These Qur'anic texts appear to be walking and moving in the real world.

It should be remembered that the Qur'an is not merely a book of recitation and scholarly discussion. That work has been done enough; this is a life, a life bounding and moving forward. It is guidance for new events with new instructions. Whenever any heart understands these texts, walks alongside them, and responds to them, the springs of power hidden within these texts burst forth. This is the secret of this Book, that within it are reservoirs of explosive strength.

A person reads one verse a thousand times, then he encounters a situation and an event, and when he reads that very verse, it is not the same verse. It is a completely new verse. It tells him what it did not tell before, or what he did not understand before. It begins to answer astonishing questions. It resolves complex difficulties. It shows a clear path. It fixes a direction, and it converts the heart from wavering into firm resolve in that matter, and the reader attains complete satisfaction.

Lesson No. 189, Explanation of the Verses
9 ... to ... 27

The Qur'an begins this surah thus: O believers, remember how these armies gathered against you and intended to uproot you from the root, and Allah, out of His mere grace and through His special hosts, turned them back disappointed. Thus, in the very first verse, the nature of the event, its beginning and its end, have been described, so that the mind may be settled that Allah's purpose is that you follow Allah, His Messenger (ﷺ) and the revelation, rely upon Him, and do not obey the disbelievers and hypocrites, and that Allah is the supporter and helper of those who act upon Allah's call and His system against the disbelievers and hypocrites.

﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when there came to you soldiers and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.﴾ (33:9)

Thus, in this general beginning, the beginning and end of the battle have been recorded, and the elements that were decisive in this battle have also been stated: namely, the gathering of the confederates and their attack, the storm of wind and rain and the other divine hosts that were not visible, and Allah's help which was based on Allah's knowledge and planning, and He was continuously watching. Now, the details:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 10–13:

اذ جاء وکم من فوقکم ۔۔۔۔۔۔ یریدون الا فرارا (10 – 13)

This was the terrifying situation that shook Madinah to its foundations. Every person was afflicted with fear and anguish. Not a single person was untouched by this situation. The Quraysh and their allies and dependents, the Banu Ghatafan and the tribes under their influence, and the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayzah had all come up from every direction, from above and from below. The circumstances were such that their fear was not separate from one heart to another. The difference that existed lay in the reaction. There was a difference in certainty concerning Allah. There was a difference in conduct, values, the concept of causes, and the manifestation of results. This is why it was an all-encompassing trial, and it completely separated the believers from the hypocrites.

Today, when we examine our own circumstances, we stand in the very same position. The circumstances are the same, the impressions are the same, the doubts are the same, the actions are the same, and within the mirror of these texts we see our faces clearly. We look, and this scene is clearly visible to us.

﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾ (33:10). And after this, the effects of this position upon people: ﴿And when the eyes became dazed and the hearts reached the throats﴾ (33:10). This is a most complete picture of a person who is afflicted with extreme constriction, fear and anguish. In this picture, both the condition of the face and the movement of the hearts are shown.

﴿And you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ (33:10). No details of these assumptions are given. By leaving them general, all agitation, all doubts and all evil feelings have been included within it. The detail of assumptions will differ in different hearts. Now let us further unfold this terrifying situation, and bring forward its features and its movements.

﴿There the believers were tried and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ (33:11). The fear that shakes the believers must necessarily be very intense and terrifying.

Muhammad ibn Maslamah and others narrated that during the Battle of the Trench, our nights were also like days, as the polytheists had set up a rotation for themselves. One day Abu Sufyan ibn Harb would come with his companions to fight, another day Khalid ibn al-Walid would come with his companions, another day Amr ibn al-As would come, another day Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb would come, another day Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl would come, and another day Dirar ibn al-Khattab. Until this calamity grew very great and intense fear spread among the people.

Al-Maqrizi, in his book Imta' al-Asma', depicted the condition of the Muslims thus: "The polytheists attacked suddenly at the break of dawn, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prepared his companions. The fighting continued that day until part of the night, and neither the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor any of the believers could move from their place. The Messenger ﷺ could not perform the Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha prayers. His companions said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have not prayed.' ﴿Then they would have been invited to fitnah (apostasy)﴾ (33:14). That is, they would have been demanded to become apostates, and these people would have immediately become apostates, without any delay and without any hesitation.

﴿But only briefly﴾: that is, if they had delayed, they would have delayed only a little, or only a few of them would have hesitated, i.e., they would have paused for a short while to think before apostatizing. This is the picture of a loose faith and conviction. This is a deep weakness, and with it they cannot withstand the confrontation. Thus the Qur'an reveals their reality and lifts the veil from their inner condition. After this, they are accused of having broken their covenant and violated their promise. With whom was this covenant? They had made this covenant with Allah, that they would not flee. This had already happened to them before.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 15:

ولقد کانوا عاھدوا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ عھد اللہ مسئولا (15)

Ibn Hisham, in his Sirah, transmits the narration of Ibn Ishaq that these people were the Banu Harithah. These were the same people who wanted to flee on the day of Uhud, and the Banu Salamah and they both had decided to turn back. But afterwards they had made a covenant with Allah that they would certainly not do such a thing. Here they are reminded that you yourselves made this covenant with Allah, that you would not do such a thing again.

On the day of Uhud, by the grace and favour of Allah, they had escaped. Allah had granted them steadfastness and had saved them from the consequences of flight. In the early period, this was one of the lessons of jihad, but today a long time has passed for the Islamic movement, and considerable experience has been gained. Therefore the Qur'an makes a harsh comment upon them.

Today, when they have broken their covenant, having broken it to avoid danger and to flee from a state of fear, the Qur'an tells them, and tells them at all times, what the supreme value is in the Islamic ideology of life, and what the concept of death and life is in the Islamic conception of life. Is flight and breach of covenant a guarantee of life?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 16–17:

Qul lan yanfa'akum ... wa la nasiran (16–17)

The reality is that all events occur in accordance with Allah's system of qada and qadar (divine decree and predestination). The system of qada and qadar carries these events and their consequences forward, and every matter reaches its end according to this system. Death and killing are a decree of destiny, and there is no escape from them. It comes at its appointed time; it does not come a moment earlier or later. Flight does not postpone death. If someone runs away from the battle, he will die his own death, and its time is very near. Every span of the world is indeed near, and all the provisions of the world are also few. There is no one to save, except that Allah's will may stand in the way of someone's death. It is Allah who decides evil for some and good for others. Apart from Allah there is no guardian and no helper. There is no one who can save anyone from the decree of Allah. Therefore, submission is submission, obedience is obedience, and fidelity is fidelity, whether it is in a time of ease or in a time of hardship. All matters are in the hand of Allah. One should place one's trust in Allah. He does what He wills.

Now the discourse turns toward those who create obstacles in the battle, who sit down heedless of jihad, and who also prevent others from jihad and say:

La maqama lakum fa-irji'u (33:13) "There is no place for you to stay, so return!" And their strange picture is drawn here. This picture, while being a true picture, is also an excellent cartoon, and such people are found in every age: cowardly, retreating, shouting and wailing very loudly, lamenting in severe circumstances, and speaking sharply and boldly in peaceful circumstances, stingy in every matter of goodness, fleeing from struggle, and becoming agitated at once if there is even the slightest threat of fear, even if it is distant. The Qur'an's manner of expression is so captivating that no color of this picture can be changed. Just read it yourselves in the Qur'anic style:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 18:

﴿Qad ya'lamu Allahu al-mu'awwiqina...﴾ to ﴿ma qatalu illa qalilan﴾ (18–20) "...". Those who take part in the fighting only for the sake of showing their names, who are extremely stingy in supporting you. When the time of danger comes, they look at you with rolling eyes, as if someone in the throes of death has fainted. But when the danger passes, these same people, greedy for benefits, come to greet you with tongues flashing like scissors. These people have never truly believed, so Allah has made all their deeds fruitless. And for Allah this is very easy. They think that the attacking army has not yet left. And if the attacking army should return, they wish they could sit somewhere in the desert among the Bedouins and keep asking about your circumstances from there. Even if they remain among you, they will take little part in the fighting.

The beginning is as follows: Allah knows well those who hinder people from war and place obstacles in the way of His cause. They advise their brothers not to take part in the war but to remain sitting in their homes.

﴿Wa la ya'tuna al-ba'sa illa qalilan﴾ (33:18). They take part in jihad only to make a show and to have their names entered. In the sight of Allah these are known people, and their deceptions are also known. Now Allah, with His miraculous pen, writes very beautifully the features of these people and of people like them:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 19:

﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ (33:19) "Grudging towards you." Their hearts are filled with spite and enmity against the Muslims. They are stingy in jihad, stingy in giving financial help, and stingy in good intentions and good desires.

﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ الْخَوْفُ ... عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ﴾ (33:19) "So when fear comes, you see them looking to you, their eyes rolling like one over whom death has come." This is a clear picture whose features are distinct and whose limbs are in motion, yet with these characteristics the picture is ridiculous. It drips with their cowardice: so terrified that their limbs tremble from fear and a shudder runs through their whole body. But when the fear departs, their picture becomes even more ridiculous.

﴿فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ الْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُم بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾ (33:19) "But when fear departs, they assail you with sharp tongues." They come out of their holes, and their voices rise, although previously a tremor had overcome them. The veins of their necks swell and they consider themselves very great. Earlier they had shrunk; now they have puffed up and, without shame or modesty, make long claims that "we endured these and these hardships, fought these and these battles, performed these and these virtuous deeds, and displayed such courage and bravery"... and then these people.

﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَى الْخَيْرِ﴾ (33:19) "Grudging towards good." They spend nothing on any good work: neither their strength, nor their deeds, nor their wealth, nor their lives... although they make very grand claims. Their tongues are sharp and they consider themselves very great. People of this kind are not confined to any one nation or tribe; they are always found in every society. Such people are very brave, eloquent and challenging when there is peace. But if there is fear and severe danger, they become stingy, cowardly, silent, and remain behind. Such people are very stingy in every good and every benefit; they merely take part in every matter verbally.

﴿أُولَئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا فَأَحْبَطَ اللَّهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ (33:19) "Those have not believed, so Allah has made their deeds fruitless." The first cause of their hypocrisy is that faith has not descended into their hearts, and they have not sought their path by the light of faith. These people do not walk upon the ways of faith. Therefore Allah has rendered their deeds void, and they do not succeed, because the real substance of success is not in their possession.

﴿وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ (33:19) "And that is easy for Allah." For Allah no task is difficult; just understand that their deeds have been lost. As for what their condition was on the Day of the Confederates (Yawm al-Ahzab) and what their thinking was...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 20:

﴿They think the confederates have not yet withdrawn.﴾ (33:20)

It is as if these people are still trembling, still hiding from the battle, still holding others back, and cannot believe that the confederates have fled, that the fear has ended, and that peace and security have returned.

﴿And if the confederates should come [again]...﴾ (33:20) ... ﴿...[they would wish that] they were out in the desert among the Bedouins, asking about your news.﴾ (33:20)

What a serious jest this is, and how grotesque a picture of these people it presents, like a cartoon. If the confederates were to attack again, these people would wish that they were not the people of Madinah, but were far away among the desert Bedouins, not sharing in the life and responsibilities of the people of Madinah. They would wish not to know what is happening there, to have no knowledge of it, and to ask others about the condition of the people of Madinah in the manner a stranger asks about a stranger, having no personal connection with them. These cowards slip away to save their lives. These people make such ridiculous wishes. They are far from the battle, they do not personally take part in this confrontation, nor do they directly touch the matter. They are afraid even from afar, and even while being so distant they still wail and lament.

﴿And they would not fight except a little.﴾ (33:20) This is the final line, and with its drawing the picture is completed. This is the picture of the hypocrites who lived within the new Islamic community that had arisen in the blessed city of Madinah. Such people join every movement that rises until the Day of Resurrection; these are the features of the hypocrites of every age. The picture ends here, and the contempt, the hatred, and the distance from them are firmly established in the hearts of the believers. These people also become lightweight in the sight of Allah and fall in the eyes of the people.

This was the condition of those who were hypocrites, in whose hearts was a disease, who spread discouragement within the Islamic ranks. This was their repugnant picture. But the terrifying, shaking fear of the Battle of the Confederates and its harsh circumstances did not make everyone so repugnant. Amid those dark and anguished conditions there were also bright faces. In those shaking circumstances there were people who stood firm like a mountain, who had complete trust in their Lord, who were content with Allah's decrees, and who were certain that Allah's help would come, despite the fact that outwardly the circumstances were extremely hopeless and fear and dismay spread on every side.

Now the Qur'an presents the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as a model, and opens this album of luminous faces with him. Look at the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

﴿Verily, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much﴾ (33:21).

Despite this frightening fear and these life-threatening circumstances, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a source of peace and tranquility for the people, and his person was a source of trust, reassurance and hope. The role that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ played in this difficult time is, in truth, an example and model for the leaders of all Islamic movements. It is an excellent pattern for all those who work purely for the pleasure of Allah and the Day of Judgment, and who wish to prove themselves the best of leaders, who remember Allah at all times and never forget Him. We should give here some glimpses of the position that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took in this battle. It is not possible to give all the details here.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out of his house and began digging the trench along with the ordinary Muslims. He would dig the earth with a pickaxe, gather the soil with a shovel, and then load it into baskets and cast it on the edges. Whoever worked would recite rajaz (rhythmic verses), and he too would join them. These people would recite the rajaz loudly, repeating the last word of the rajaz. They sang simple songs related to the events of that time. There was a man named Ju'ayl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not like this name, so he changed his name and named him Amr. Then the Muslims made a rajaz about him, very simple:

Sammahu min ba'di Ju'aylin 'Amran, wa kana lil-ba'isi yawman zuhra.

When the Muslims would recite this rajaz and say "Amra," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would also respond by saying "Amra," and when they recited the word "zuhra" in the second phrase, he too would repeat "zuhra" in response to them. Now think about this atmosphere and imagine this enthusiasm: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is repeating the closing words of the rajaz, "Amra" and "zuhra," and at the same time striking with the pickaxe, gathering soil with the shovel, carrying the soil in baskets, and responding to the rajaz. This conduct would have filled every hair on the bodies of those people with strength. How filled with power and courage would their spirits have been, and how much boldness, courage, confidence and honor would they have been receiving!

Zayd ibn Thabit was carrying soil, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "This is an excellent young man." He fell asleep and slept right there in the trench. Due to the very great cold... Hadrat Umarah ibn Hazm secretly took his weapons, and he did not even notice. When he woke up, the weapons were gone, and he became distressed. Upon this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Abu Amad (father of the one who sleeps much), you slept so much that your weapon has gone!" Then he said to give it back, and after that he ordered that a Muslim's property should not be hidden even as a joke. This incident also shows that among the Islamic ranks were people who were alert in mind and watchful, and the eye of the Messenger ﷺ was on everyone, whether small or great. It also shows that serious humor and good cheer remained with the leader of the revolution even in these difficult circumstances. "O father of the sleeper, you slept and your weapon went!" And this shows the conditions the Muslims were in and how close they were to the Prophet ﷺ.

The spirit of the Prophet ﷺ was seeing the signs of the Islamic revolution far and wide. Even in the glint of the stones, Allah showed the Prophet ﷺ the vastness of the Islamic revolution. From the very first day, he had given the good news that the treasures of Caesar and Chosroes would come into your hands. But even in the disheartening circumstances of the Battle of the Confederates, when a spark came out of the stone from the blow of the pickaxe, the Prophet ﷺ would be shown the picture of the future through it, and he would immediately tell the Muslims, and because of this springs of certainty and hope would burst forth in their hearts.

Ibn Ishaq writes: The narration of Salman al-Farsi has reached me that he said: I was digging a corner of the trench when a stone became difficult for me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was near me at that time. He saw that I was striking continuously and the place had become difficult for me. The Messenger ﷺ came down, took the pickaxe from my hand and struck the stone. A spark rose from beneath the pickaxe. Then he struck a second blow, and again a spark rose from the stone. Then he struck a third blow, and again a spark rose from the stone. He said: I asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what was that light I saw, that when you strike, the pickaxe flashes?" The Messenger ﷺ said, "Salman, have you seen this?" I said, "Yes." He said: In the first spark it was shown to me that Yemen had been conquered for me. In the second spark it was shown that Allah had conquered for me the lands of Syria and the West. And in the third spark there was the matter that Allah had conquered the East for me.

Maqrizi has written that this incident happened to Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and at that time Salman al-Farsi was also present. The lesson for us in this is that even in such a frightening environment, the hearts and minds of the Muslims were full of confidence.

Remember also the time when Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), in severe cold, came out from the enemy's camp. He had information. He was trembling from the cold, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying wrapped in a long shawl belonging to one of his wives. The Messenger ﷺ was in prayer, in intimate communion with his Lord. He did not leave Hudhayfah alone to keep trembling until the Messenger ﷺ finished praying; rather, he drew Hudhayfah in between his legs and threw a corner of his shawl over him so that he would become warm, and he continued his prayer. The prayer ended. Hudhayfah gave the Messenger ﷺ the information and gave him the good news, because... Mubarak was saying that something was going to happen today. Hudhayfah came back after seeing it.

As for the courage, steadfastness and reliance on Allah of the Messenger ﷺ, these are evident from his biography, and are entirely evident from this whole story. They are well known, so we cannot give details here. Allah spoke the truth: "Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah there is an excellent example for you, for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much."

After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, now behold the picture of a true believer, who fully relies on Allah and is completely content. This picture is bright, radiant and beautiful. See how this believer stands firm against every kind of terrifying circumstance. He plunges into dangers. He stands firm like a rock in dangerous situations in which ordinary people are seized with trembling, and the more severe the danger, the more he has of tranquility, greater reliance on Allah, and certainty of good news.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 22:

ولما را المؤمنون ۔۔۔۔۔ ایمانا وتسلیما (23) ” “۔

The fear that the Muslims were afflicted with in this battle was so great, the grief that reached them in this ghazwa (military campaign) was so severe, and the restlessness they suffered in this event was so intense, that they were shaken. The Qur'an used the expression zilzalan shadidan (33:11) for this. Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿There the believers were tested, and they were shaken with a severe shaking.﴾ (33:11)

These people were human beings after all, and human endurance is inherently limited. Allah does not burden a human being beyond his capacity. Although they had complete certainty that the final victory would be theirs, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had given them good tidings, and these tidings were not only of the conquest of Arabia but also of Yemen, Syria, and the East and the West, yet despite these realities, the terrifying circumstances of the moment had shaken them to the core, and they continually felt anguish and fear.

The picture of the condition of the Companions and how frightened they were becomes very clear from the narration of Hadhrat Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. The state of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their inner condition: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the Companions: Who is there who will stand up and go and find out, within the army of the enemy, what they are doing? The condition for him is that he will return. I will supplicate to Allah that He keeps him with me in Paradise." Despite the guarantee of his return and the guarantee of his being with the Prophet in Paradise through the supplication, no one rose on their own. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) repeated it three times. Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman by name, and Hudhayfah (ra) also said that when his name was called, there was no option left for him but to go. The reality is that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could only adopt this stance in a state of extreme fear. It appears that this matter was beyond their strength.

Yet despite this severe shaking, and despite eyes being fixed in terror and the anxiety of their lives, these people had an unbroken bond with Allah. They knew the Sunan of Allah (the divine laws) to such an extent that they were never hidden from their sight, and they had unwavering trust in the Sunan of Allah, that these Sunan are unchangeable, and when the causes are provided in accordance with them, the results will certainly come out in accordance with them. This is why the believers understood that after this intense fear and shaking, the divine help was now near, because they knew that Allah had said:

﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you? They were touched by adversity and hardship and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.﴾ (2:214)

And since they had been shaken, the divine help was near. For this reason they said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us," and "The word of Allah and His Messenger was true." (This event increased their faith and submission.)

﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us﴾ (33:22): "This is what Allah and the Messenger ﷺ had promised us." This fear, this restlessness, this trembling, and this constriction are the things upon which the promise of help was made to us. Therefore, help is about to come.

﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ (33:22): That is, the signs that Allah and the Messenger had set for the arrival of divine help were true, and now that those signs are appearing, they are also true. This is why their hearts became content with the coming of Allah's help.

﴿And it increased them only in faith and submission﴾ (33:22): "This event increased their faith and submission."

Nevertheless, they were human beings and mortals, and they could not be free of human emotions. Human weaknesses also clung to them. Sharia did not require of them that they bear a burden greater than a human being. They had to remain within the bounds of humanity. And it was the wisdom of Allah that the distinctive qualities and signs of the Sharia be found within them. They were created so that they would act as humans and not be any other kind of creation: neither angels nor devils, neither animals nor stones. They were human, and therefore fear would overcome them, they would be troubled with anxiety, and they would feel constriction. When the danger exceeded the limit of their endurance, trembling would also overtake them. But despite these weaknesses, they were attached to a strong rope. They were bound to Allah, and Allah was protecting them from falling. He would again create hopes within them and save them from despair. Therefore, they were a unique example in the history of humanity, an example for which no second example is found, and for which there is no parallel. We should recognize this reality so that we know that among all the people of human history there was also such a model, and that humanity once reached this standard. They were humans, not angels; they had weaknesses and they also had strength; and their honour and standard is that they raised humanity to such a lofty level that, while remaining within the bounds of humanity, they reached such a high standard.

When we see that weakness has entered us, or our steps have become unsteady, or we have become frightened, or a time of constriction has come upon us, or we have fallen into terrifying and dangerous circumstances, we should not lose hope, and we should not begin lamentation and crying out that we are finished. But nor should we adopt the position that these weaknesses existed even in the best of generations, that they are part of our nature, and that we are even among those who are better than all other people, because there is also a strong rope. This strong rope is the rope of connection to the heavens. We should hold on to Allah, return to the rope of His support, trust and assurance, and when our steps become unsteady, we should understand that the help of Allah is coming, so that we remain steadfast, attain stability, and once again set out on the path of truth with the greatest strength.

In the early period of Islam, Allah had formed the team of the Companions of the Noble Messenger, and this very balance had been granted to them. This was a unique team. The Qur'an itself repeatedly praises this team for the feats they accomplished and how they remained steadfast. Some of them have already reached Allah, and others are awaiting.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 23:

﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who still waits, and they have not changed in the least.﴾ (33:23-24)

This example stands in contrast to that repugnant example, in which people had made a covenant with Allah that they would not turn their backs, but afterwards they did not keep their covenant.

﴿And the covenant with Allah will be questioned about.﴾ (33:15)

Imam Ahmad narrated from Thabit that: "My paternal uncle Anas ibn Nadr (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) was unable to be present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Badr. This was very hard upon him. He used to say: 'This was the first battle in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took part, and I was absent. If Allah grants me the opportunity to take part with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in some battle, Allah will see what I do.' No one other than him said such a thing. He was present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud. He came before Saʿd ibn Muʿadh (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) and said to him: 'Abu ʿUmar! Wah! Wah! The fragrance of Paradise! I smell it coming from Uhud.' It is said that he fought against them and was martyred. There were more than eighty wounds on his body from arrows, swords and spears. His sister, my paternal aunt Rabiʿ bint Nadr, said: 'I recognised my brother only by the tips of his fingers.' She said that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah.﴾ (33:23)"

The Companions (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhum) were of the view that this verse was revealed concerning Anas ibn Nadr and his companions. This is a most radiant picture of incomparable believers. We mention it here so that it becomes clear what the reality of faith is, and what hypocrisy is, what fulfilment of a covenant is, and what breaking a covenant is. This was a comparative study within the training ground of the battlefield. After this, it is explained why Allah places His servants in such trials, what the end of those who do not keep their covenant is, and what the end of those who surrender themselves entirely to Allah is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 24:

﴿Liyajzi Allahu as-sadiqina...﴾ to ﴿kana ghafuran rahiman﴾ (33:22)

The Qur'an frequently offers commentary on events and occurrences. The purpose is to show that all matters are in Allah's control. The wisdom behind these events is also explained, so that no event occurs in vain or without purpose. Every event is part of divine wisdom and comes at its appointed time. Behind it lies purposeful planning, and it produces its determined results. In it, mercy and grace for the servants of Allah become manifest, and one should know that Allah's mercy and His grace are always manifest.

﴿Inna Allaha kana ghafuran rahiman﴾ (33:24): "Indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." And this great event concludes with the fact that the belief the believers held about their Lord proved correct, while the hypocrites and those who spread rumours held mistaken notions. In short, the values of faith ultimately prevailed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 25:

"And Allah turned back those who disbelieved, in their rage, not having obtained any good. And Allah sufficed for the believers in the fighting. And ever is Allah Strong and Exalted in Might." (33:25)

This battle began, advanced, and reached its conclusion, yet throughout the whole course of events the reins were in the hands of Allah. He turned the course of events as He willed. The Qur'an, through its manner of expression, reveals this reality: whatever events occurred, Allah brought them about, and this fact was firmly implanted in the hearts of the believers. In this way the Islamic conception of life was made clear.

Now the consequences of this military expedition did not fall only upon the idolatrous Quraysh and Ghatafan, but the allies of the idolaters, Banu Qurayzah, also came within its grip.

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who backed them from their fortresses ... over all things competent.﴾ (26–27)

When he came, riding a donkey which they had prepared well for him, the Aws began to fall at his feet, saying: "O Sa'd, we are your friends. Show kindness to them." They were pleading with him to soften his heart towards them. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh remained silent and said nothing. When they insisted, he replied that the time had come for Sa'd, in the matter of Allah, not to fear the blame of any blamer. Thus they realised that Sa'd was not going to give a fair judgement.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 26–29 (part 2 of 2):

When Sa'd went to the tent that was the Messenger of Allah's tent, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Stand up to receive and honour your chief." The Muslims stood up and brought him down, with great honour, respect and hospitality, so that his decision would be carried out well.

When Sa'd sat down, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "These people have surrendered at the signal of Banu Qurayzah to your judgment. So command concerning them whatever you wish." Sa'd said, "Will my command be enforced upon them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." "And will it be enforced upon all those who are in this tent?" He (ﷺ) said, "Yes." Then Sa'd said, "And upon those who are there as well?" (At this point Sa'd pointed to the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he himself turned his face away out of modesty, honour and respect.) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Yes."

Then Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I decide that their fighting men be put to death, and that their property and children be made spoils of war." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have indeed judged according to the command of Allah, and Allah had decreed this judgment above the seven heavens."

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that trenches be dug in the ground, and these people were brought bound. Their necks were struck off. They were some seven or eight hundred men. Those among the men and women who had not reached puberty were taken as slaves. Among the slain was Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who had shut himself up in the fortress with them in accordance with the agreement.

From that time the Jews were humiliated, and from that day on the movement of hypocrisy in Medina grew weak. The heads of the hypocrites were lowered, and they became fearful of what they had previously been doing. The result was that after that day the disbelievers did not dare to attack the Muslims. Rather, from then on, the attacks were launched by the Muslims, until Makkah and Ta'if were conquered.

It can be said that the schemes of the Jews, the polytheists of Makkah and the hypocrites were interwoven, and when the Jews were expelled from Medina, these intrigues came to an end, and from that day the foundation of the Islamic state became firm. This is the background to the divine words:

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported the invaders from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts, so that a party of them you killed and a party you took captive. And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trampled. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (33:26–27)

"Sayasi" (fortresses) means castles. The land that the Muslims had not trampled was the land of Banu Qurayzah, which was their possession, around their quarter. This land too came into the hands of the Muslims along with their wealth. It may also be indicated that Banu Qurayzah handed over the land without fighting, and "trampling" means battle. And Allah is over all things competent.

﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, competent﴾ (33:27). From all these events the conclusion is drawn that Allah is over all things competent; that is, all affairs are in the hands of Allah. In this whole account, all matters are attributed to Allah, and all events are presented as the result of His power, so that Allah, through events and then through the revelation of the Qur'an, establishes in the hearts of the rest of the Muslims the Islamic conception of life, so that it may settle clear and pure in their hearts.

Thus this great event concluded here. Within it, numerous divine laws (sunan ilahiyyah, the constant patterns of Allah's dealings), numerous lofty values, numerous guidances and numerous principles were set forth, so that these matters might become clear and become part of the life of the Muslim community. Thus these events are good material for training, and by placing them in the Qur'an they have been made a standard and guide for the Islamic model of life. These verses were declared to be the direction of the Islamic community, and their concepts were firmly settled within their lives. Lofty values were made clear for the Islamic community, and in these trials and tests the Islamic character was written and came into view.

Abd Allah ibn Rawaha and Khawwat ibn Jubayr also went with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Go and see whether the reports reaching us are true or not. If these reports are true, then report to me in such words that only I understand them, so that the Muslims are not adversely affected. But if they remain faithful, then announce it openly." (From this it becomes clear how the Prophet (ﷺ) understood the effect this news would have on people.)

When the delegation went, they found that these people were in an even worse position than the reports had indicated. They reviled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Who is the Messenger? Whom are you talking about? There is no covenant or agreement between us and Muhammad." The delegation returned and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by means of gestures. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu Akbar! O Muslims, be given the glad tidings!" (The Prophet (ﷺ) said these words to make the Muslims steadfast.)

Ibn Ishaq says: Now the calamity doubled. It spread widely. Enemies came from above and below, and doubts arose in the hearts of the Muslims. Some hypocrites came out openly. This was the situation before the Battle of Uhud. But when the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) received Allah's help in the Battle of the Confederates, and the enemies of the Muslims returned frustrated and defeated, gaining nothing, Allah Himself fought on behalf of the believers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Madinah victorious. The people began to put down their weapons. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because of the continuous state of war, began to bathe. He was in the house of Umm Salamah when Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him: "O Messenger of Allah, have you put down your weapons?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." Jibril said: "But the angels have not put down their weapons, and I have just returned from pursuing that people." Then Jibril said: "Allah commands you: proceed to the Banu Qurayza." The Banu Qurayza were several miles from Madinah. This event took place after the Zuhr prayer. The Prophet (ﷺ) gave the order: "No one should pray except in the territory of Banu Qurayza." The people set out. On the way, the time for the Asr prayer arrived. Some people prayed on the road, and they said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had intended only that they hurry. But others said: "We will not pray except in the lands of the Banu Qurayza." Yet no one blamed the others for this. The Prophet (ﷺ) arrived after them. In Madinah, Ibn Umm Maktum was appointed as the governor, [Surah Abasa:] ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him﴾ (80:1–2). The standard was given to Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). The Prophet (ﷺ) besieged them for twenty-five days and told them to lay down their arms. When the matter dragged on for them, they laid down their arms upon the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, chief of the Aws. In the Jahiliyyah, these people had been among his allies. They thought that he would show them kindness, just as Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had done with his friends and had got them released from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They thought that Sa'd ibn Mu'adh would do the same as Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had done. They did not know that an arrow had struck Sa'd in the major vein of his arm, and if that vein were cut, the wounded man would never recover. This had happened in the early days of the Trench. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had cauterised his wound and had kept him in a tent inside the mosque, so that the Prophet (ﷺ) could tend to him conveniently. Sa'd used to pray: "O Allah, if You have yet decreed further battles between us and the Quraysh, then keep me alive. But if the war between us and them has ended, then let this wound keep bleeding. And my only wish is that my eyes be comforted regarding the Banu Qurayza." Allah accepted his prayer, and decreed that they would surrender to his judgement, and that this request was made by them of their own accord.

Now the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Sa'd from Madinah so that he might decide regarding these people. When he came, riding a donkey which they had prepared well for him, the Aws began to fall at his feet, saying: "O Sa'd, we are your friends. Show kindness to them." They were pleading with him to soften his heart towards them. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh remained silent and said nothing. When they insisted, he replied that the time had come for Sa'd, in the matter of Allah, not to fear the blame of any blamer. Thus they realised that Sa'd was not going to give a fair judgement.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 26–29 (part 2 of 2):

When Sa'd went to the tent that was the Messenger of Allah's tent, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Stand up to receive and honour your chief." The Muslims stood up and brought him down, with great honour, respect and hospitality, so that his decision would be carried out well.

When Sa'd sat down, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "These people have surrendered at the signal of Banu Qurayzah to your judgment. So command concerning them whatever you wish." Sa'd said, "Will my command be enforced upon them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." "And will it be enforced upon all those who are in this tent?" He (ﷺ) said, "Yes." Then Sa'd said, "And upon those who are there as well?" (At this point Sa'd pointed to the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he himself turned his face away out of modesty, honour and respect.) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Yes."

Then Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I decide that their fighting men be put to death, and that their property and children be made spoils of war." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have indeed judged according to the command of Allah, and Allah had decreed this judgment above the seven heavens."

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that trenches be dug in the ground, and these people were brought bound. Their necks were struck off. They were some seven or eight hundred men. Those among the men and women who had not reached puberty were taken as slaves. Among the slain was Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who had shut himself up in the fortress with them in accordance with the agreement.

From that time the Jews were humiliated, and from that day on the movement of hypocrisy in Medina grew weak. The heads of the hypocrites were lowered, and they became fearful of what they had previously been doing. The result was that after that day the disbelievers did not dare to attack the Muslims. Rather, from then on, the attacks were launched by the Muslims, until Makkah and Ta'if were conquered.

It can be said that the schemes of the Jews, the polytheists of Makkah and the hypocrites were interwoven, and when the Jews were expelled from Medina, these intrigues came to an end, and from that day the foundation of the Islamic state became firm. This is the background to the divine words:

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported the invaders from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts, so that a party of them you killed and a party you took captive. And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trampled. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (33:26–27)

"Sayasi" (fortresses) means castles. The land that the Muslims had not trampled was the land of Banu Qurayzah, which was their possession, around their quarter. This land too came into the hands of the Muslims along with their wealth. It may also be indicated that Banu Qurayzah handed over the land without fighting, and "trampling" means battle. And Allah is over all things competent.

﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, competent﴾ (33:27). From all these events the conclusion is drawn that Allah is over all things competent; that is, all affairs are in the hands of Allah. In this whole account, all matters are attributed to Allah, and all events are presented as the result of His power, so that Allah, through events and then through the revelation of the Qur'an, establishes in the hearts of the rest of the Muslims the Islamic conception of life, so that it may settle clear and pure in their hearts.

Thus this great event concluded here. Within it, numerous divine laws (sunan ilahiyyah, the constant patterns of Allah's dealings), numerous lofty values, numerous guidances and numerous principles were set forth, so that these matters might become clear and become part of the life of the Muslim community. Thus these events are good material for training, and by placing them in the Qur'an they have been made a standard and guide for the Islamic model of life. These verses were declared to be the direction of the Islamic community, and their concepts were firmly settled within their lives. Lofty values were made clear for the Islamic community, and in these trials and tests the Islamic character was written and came into view.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 30–31:

"O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality..." (33:30–31) ""

This is the demand of the lofty station they occupy. They are the wives of the Master of both worlds (ﷺ). They have been given the rank of the Mothers of the Believers (Ummahat al-Mu'minin), and these two honours place upon them very weighty responsibilities. Their first requirement is that you abstain completely from all immoralities (fawahish). Even if, by way of hypothetical supposition, any one of them were to commit immorality, she would be given double punishment. The purpose of this hypothetical threat is in fact to show how exalted their station is and what the demands of that station are.

"And that is ever easy for Allah" (33:30) ""This is easy for Allah." Despite being the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), nobody can prevent Allah from punishing you. It may come to mind that there might be some obstacle to punishing the wives of the Messenger, the Trusted (ﷺ); therefore this notion was refuted.

"And whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness" (33:31) ""And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and does righteous deeds." Qunut means obedience and humble submission (khushu'), and righteous deed is the correct translation of qunut.

"We will give her reward twice" (33:31) ""We will give her her reward twice." Just as, if any of them commits immorality, her punishment will be doubled, likewise her reward will be doubled.

"And We have prepared for her a noble provision" (33:31) ""And We have prepared for her a generous provision." It is present and ready; after the double reward there is an additional noble provision, which will be the grace and generosity of Allah.

After this it is explained that the wives of the Prophet are not like ordinary women; therefore, in relation to people they have certain obligations, and in serving Allah they also have certain obligations. They also have obligations within the home. It is stated that Allah Himself is the guardian of this great household. Allah wishes to purify the life of this family. They are told that concerning the wisdom and the divine verses being revealed within your homes, you bear special responsibilities, and this domestic environment distinguishes you from all the wives and women of the worlds.
