Yes, there is kinship between me and you, and I shall continue to fulfil its right." (Muslim, Tirmidhi)

When they were made aware of their dignity and station, and that they could reach this station only through *taqwa*, then Allah Almighty explains the means through which Allah wishes to purify the People of the Prophet's House completely and clean them thoroughly, and their complete purification is kept in view.

*Fala takhda'na bil-qawli fa-yatma'a alladhi fi qalbihi maradun* (33:32): "So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire."

Allah gives the Mothers of the Believers the first command: when they have to speak with men who are not their *mahram* (those they may not marry), their speech should not have that softness which, if they speak in a gentle and soft voice, would be a cause of sensual stimulation for the listener. For generally, soft words produce appetite in men. They are stirred by them, and people with sick hearts and weak morals can bring evil thoughts into their hearts.

Consider here who the women are whom Allah is warning. They are the Mothers of the Believers, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, about whom no one could even imagine such a thing or entertain any desire, and upon whom no sickness of any sick person could have any effect. Outwardly, a person could think only this. Then, in what age is this admonition given? In the age of the Prophet ﷺ, in the age of those outstanding and chosen Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), whose equals neither came before them nor after them. But the real point is this: the God who created men and women knew that if a woman speaks in a soft and gentle voice, with coquetry and charm, she can produce wrong thoughts in people's hearts and create temptation within their hearts. Especially hearts that were already diseased can quickly be provoked, and such diseased hearts are present in every age and era. In every society such people are found, and such diseased people can be inclined towards any woman, even if she is the honoured wife of the Last of the Prophets, one of the Mothers of the Believers. No environment can remain pure and clean unless the causes of filth are blocked.

And what is the condition of the society in which we live today? This society is already diseased, impure and debased, in which there are temptations at every step. Everywhere there are sensual allurements, and desires flutter about. In such an environment, what should we do, when lust is aroused from every side, provoked, and sexuality is heated more and more? What should we do in this society and this age? Our age is one in which women's tone is extremely seductive, their voices extremely liquid, with all the temptations of femininity gathered together, with all the temptations of sexual attraction produced, present everywhere with extremely enticing and alluring charm. Where are such women pure, and where is the atmosphere of purity? They are, through their gestures, their voices and their nakedness, implicated in all those filths from which Allah wishes to purify the Mothers of the Believers, and from which Allah wishes to purify His chosen servants. In such circumstances, how dangerous is nakedness and free mixing!

*Wa qulna qawlan ma'rufan* (33:32): "But speak a good, straightforward word."

First they were forbidden from a soft and seductive voice, and now it is said that they should speak plain and simple speech, in a customary manner, as a stranger man and a stranger woman ordinarily speak with one another. In these words there should be nothing improper. Sometimes the subject of conversation can itself incite to wantonness more than a soft tone. Therefore, between a stranger man and a stranger woman there should not even be any hint of tone or manner. There should be no chit-chat between them, no joking and no frivolous talk, so that as a result there is no inclination towards other matters, and people, whether near or far, do not fall into wrong paths. Allah Almighty is the Creator, and He knows very well the temperament and nature of His creation. It is Allah who addresses the Mothers of the Believers in this way, so that they may converse with the strangers of their own age in this manner, while that age was the best of centuries (*khayr al-qurun*).

*Wa qarna fi buyutikunna* (33:33): "And remain in your houses with dignity."

*Qarna* is derived from *waqara* (وقر), which means to be heavy, to settle in one's place. Its literal meaning is not that they should be confined inside the houses and never go out of them. It is a subtle indication that the proper place of such a woman is her home. This is her settled place, and apart from it, if she is found elsewhere, that is a temporary state and an exceptional condition. She does not remain established in it. Going out must be only out of necessity.

The home (*bayt*) is the place of rest and the seat of the woman, which Allah has chosen for her by way of her creation and nature, in which she does not depart from her nature, is not involved in wrongdoing, and is not prepared by her nature for those exhausting duties in which she is caught up. Where she is occupied with that work for which Allah has in truth created her. "Islam provides a specific atmosphere for the home, so that the upbringing of children may become better and better in that atmosphere. Allah made it obligatory upon the man to provide maintenance (*nafaqah*) for his wife, so that the mother does not have to struggle for livelihood, does not have to spend her time in toil and labour, and can fully and contentedly raise her children, and enhance the order of the home, its generosity and its happiness. A woman who is exhausted and worn out by labour, who has to perform the duties of her employment, whose time and engagements lie outside the home, and whose strength is spent there, cannot possibly give joy to the home. Nor is it possible for her to fully raise weak children. Homes of working women have no more standing than hotels and bakeries. They lack the attraction that the home has. The true home is the one created by a domestic woman, and the attraction of the home is also that which springs from a good wife. The fountainhead of love in the home is the mother. A wife, a mother, or a woman who spends her time in employment can give the home nothing but constriction and grief and sorrow." (*Islam aur Alami Salamati*)

"A woman's leaving the home is a very great calamity for any household, and though occasionally it is truly necessary, if there is no need, then in that case it is a curse upon reason and wisdom. Its spread occurred in those ages in which evil, corruption and misguidance increased, and humanity suffered defeat." (*Ibid.*)

As for a woman going out without any necessity or without any employment, and men and women mixing in bazaars and streets, this is that defeat after which humanity falls into the mire of filth and man reaches the level of an animal.

In the age of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, women went out for prayer, and even now there is no legal prohibition on this. But that was an age in which people stood at the high level of chastity and purity. There was fear of Allah among people, and women went out for prayer fully veiled, such that people could not recognise them, and at that time women did not display their points of temptation at all. Even so, Hadrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) disapproved of their going out in that age.

It is related in the *Sahihayn* that Hadrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The wives of the believers used to join the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the dawn prayer. Then they would return wrapped in their veils, and because of the darkness they could not be recognised." And in the *Sahihayn* too is her narration that if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had witnessed the age in which women have invented new things, he would have forbidden them just as the women of the Children of Israel were forbidden.

The question is: what new fashion had women adopted in the time of Hadrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her)? And what changes were there that, had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seen them, he would have forbidden women from prayer? Just consider: that was the best of centuries, and today see where we stand.

*Wa la tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula* (33:33): "And do not display yourselves as in the former times of ignorance."

That is, when any of you is compelled to go out. Previously, the command to remain settled in the houses had already been given. In the Jahili age women used to display their adornment and finery, but among the narrations about this display, the forms reported are all very simple and sober. In today's age, the nakedness that women have adopted cannot be compared even with the age of Jahiliyyah.

Mujahid says: "In the Jahiliyyah, women would go out and walk among men; this was the tabarruj of the Jahiliyyah." Qatadah says: "They would walk with coquetry and affectation, and this was forbidden." Muqatil ibn Hayyan says: "Women would throw their veils over their heads, but would not wrap them so as to cover the ornaments of the neck, or conceal the ornaments of the ears; so the neck ornaments and ear ornaments would be visible."

Allamah Ibn Kathir says: "A woman would go out among men in such a way that her chest was exposed and nothing was over it; sometimes her neck and the braids of her hair were bare, and her earrings were also visible. Allah commanded the believing women not to display these things."

This was the adornment and display of the Jahiliyyah, and the Qur'an wished to purify the Islamic society from the evil traces of that time, so that all the factors of temptation would disappear from the Islamic society, and that its manners, concepts, collective consciousness and taste would become elevated and pure. In the purification of the Islamic society we have included the purification of "taste" as well, because looking at the naked human body is a taste that is extremely filthy and degraded. There is no doubt that this taste is dishonest compared with the serious, constant and organised taste of beauty. In this dishonest taste, the taste of the soul, chastity and consciousness is absent.

That is: the Islamic standard raises the human level and makes man progressed. Seriousness and dignity are in themselves a beauty. This is true beauty, but a superficial and Jahili taste is deprived of the perception and consciousness of this true beauty. Because according to the fallen Jahili taste, beauty lies only in flesh and skin, and this taste is the motive of Jahili taste. These verses of the Holy Qur'an, by pointing here to the Jahili display, show that these are the remnants of fallen Jahiliyyah, and those who have moved forward leaving the age of Jahiliyyah behind are elevated above this standard, and their consciousness and their taste of beauty are also raised above the level of Jahiliyyah. Jahiliyyah is not the name of a particular era. Time is not ignorant; people are ignorant. Jahiliyyah is the name of a state. In it people have particular concepts, and this state, these concepts and these customs can exist in every time and place.

By this standard, we today are in the age of Jahiliyyah, utterly blind Jahiliyyah, whose sensibility is filthy, whose consciousness is filthy, whose concepts are animalistic, and which likes a station sunk in filth, lower than the human station. In it there is no purity, cleanliness or blessing. Humanity is tossed about in it, and it does not desire the purification according to the standard by which Islam wishes to purify human society. It wants to remove the remnants of the first Jahiliyyah, and the Qur'an and Islam have begun this work with the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet (ﷺ), so that they may be a minaret of purity, refinement and light for the common Muslims.

The Qur'an addresses the Prophet (ﷺ) to take these measures: join the hearts of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Allah, and fix their aim on a lofty horizon, very bright and very pure, so that they gradually rise up to that shining minaret.

﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ (33:33). Servitude to Allah is nothing other than a collective pattern and collective morality; rather, servitude to Allah is the path through which a human being can rise to a high and lofty moral and collective level. Servitude to Allah is the provision for the traveller. The traveller needs to seek help for the servitude of Allah. Therefore there is need of a connection with Allah from which a person receives help, and a connection with Allah by which the heart keeps being cleansed and purified. There is need of a firm link with Allah by which a person rises above the conventional conduct of people and the customs of present society. He should have the thought and consciousness that the connection with Allah is higher and more exalted than people, the whole society, and his own family. Through this connection a feeling should arise in him to invite other people also towards the connection with Allah. It should not be that a person, although aware of the light of Islam, becomes a follower of other people, and they lead him towards darkness and gloom, which generally spreads everywhere when the connection with Allah is cut off.

Islam alone is a religion possessing every kind of ritual of worship, every kind of morality and etiquette, every kind of law and every kind of constitutional arrangement. All these matters are within the framework of a worldview, and all these matters, remaining within that framework, fulfil the objectives of the Islamic worldview. All these fields move together in harmony toward one goal, and it is through this harmony and coordination that the overall structure of the religion of Islam is formed. Without the presence and coordination of all these elements, this religion can by no means be established.

This is why it was commanded: establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ); and within obedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), all conscious direction, all moral guidance, every kind of conduct, and attitude in family and collective affairs are gathered together, because Islam cannot be established unless someone establishes these; and this collective submissiveness is for a specific purpose.

﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the uncleanness, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾ (33:33). In this expression there are many indications, all full of love, affection, ardour and tenderness. They are told: "You are the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet." The term Ahl al-Bayt is not explicitly stated, but it points to the house of the Prophet. As if in the world this is the one great household, and this household deserves this attribute. When "al-Bayt" is said, the meaning is the House of the Prophet. The same kind of indications occur in the Qur'an regarding the Ka'bah: it too is called "al-Bayt" and "al-Bayt al-Haram", and in the same sense the House of the Prophet was also called al-Bayt. As if this is the great household, this is the household.

Then this expression: O Ahl al-Bayt, Allah wishes to remove uncleanness from you completely and to purify you, that is, Allah has Himself taken upon Himself the task of purifying the household of the Prophet. Allah Ta'ala has taken upon Himself the responsibility for the purification of a house! As if this is the very lofty rank of the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet. It is He who speaks, He who created the whole universe by "Be, and it is." He is the Mighty, the Compeller, and He has power over all things; and when He wishes to do this, it is also a great honour for the Ahl al-Bayt.

Allah says this in His Book which is recited in the heavens, recited on the earth, recited in every age and every place, which millions of people have followed in every age, and whose recitation millions of people perform at every moment.

The final point is that these commands and guidelines are made here a means of purification and cleanliness, and through them this household is intended to be purified. "Tathir" derives from "tahhur"; uncleanness is removed only when one adopts means by which it is removed, and people do this themselves and purify their practical lives. People should have a consciousness of purity and be God-fearing; their conduct should be pure. They should fully enter Islam and turn their life's direction toward Islam, and their goals should be Islamic.

This discussion concludes with further guidance for the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), reminding the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) again that your station and rank are very high. You are distinguished from other women, because you are members of the household of the Master of both worlds (ﷺ). The Qur'an is being revealed in your houses, which is full of wisdom and understanding. Thus your houses are the places of descent of wisdom; the rains of the light of guidance and faith are falling there.

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom; indeed Allah is Subtle and Aware﴾ (33:34). This is the lofty rank of which merely reminding them is sufficient. Everyone perceives this exalted rank. It is a great station given by Allah and a favour to which nothing is equal. This admonition is repeated at the end of the address and speech delivered to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) at the time when they were given the choice: that you may choose the world and its transient adornments, or choose Allah, His Messenger and the Hereafter. It is shown that consider well: Allah has given you a very great blessing, and this entire life is not worth anything in comparison with it.

After the household of the Prophet, now the means of purification within the Islamic society are also explained in great detail and with precision. In this, men and women are equal.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 35:

Indeed, the men who submit and the women who submit, ... and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him, for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward (35).

All the qualities gathered together in this verse play a very important role in the training and shaping of the human soul. What are these qualities? Islam, faith, obedience to the command, truthfulness, patience, humbling oneself before Allah, giving charity, fasting, guarding one's private parts, and remembering Allah often. All these qualities are such that they are very important in building personality and forming character. Islam is the name of surrendering completely, and faith (iman) means certainty and affirmation, and there is a very deep relationship between them. Each is a form of the other. Surrendering before Allah means deep and complete affirmation, and where true affirmation exists, surrender is found automatically.

Qunut (devotion, obedience) means obedience to the command, but behind this obedience there must be faith and Islam. This obedience and its motivation should come from within; it should not be mere compulsion. It should be done with pleasure, not with reluctance. Truthfulness (sidq) is a general quality of a Muslim and a general garment. Whoever is not truthful is considered outside the Muslim community. Elsewhere it is said:

﴿Only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah fabricate lies﴾ (16:105). Liars are expelled from the ranks of Islam, because the ranks of the ummah are the ranks of the truthful.

Patience is the quality without which a Muslim and a believer cannot perform their duties at all. The believer is in constant need of patience, at every step: patience over worldly desires, patience over the difficulties faced on the path of Islamic da'wah, patience over people's harm, patience over the weaknesses, fickleness and crookedness of hearts, patience over trials, tests and difficulties, patience over happiness and sorrow. In short, in every situation, patience and seriousness are a difficult but necessary task.

Khushu' (humility) and khashyah (awe of Allah) are qualities of both the heart and the outward limbs. The meaning is that both the heart and the limbs should perceive Allah's greatness, His majesty and His grandeur, and fear Allah. Fasting has also been declared a quality of the believer. The indication is that fasting, and arranging for and welcoming it, are among the qualities of the believers. Through fasting, restraining desires and the longing for needs for a limited time is intended; patience is included in it. Firmness of willpower is also intended, and the dominance of human qualities over animal qualities is intended.

Hifz al-furuj (guarding the private parts): guarding one's private parts, thus adopting purity, and keeping control over deep natural inclinations that are part of the human self and exist deep within it. These inclinations are so strong that only those who have the help and support of Allah can control them. Then, through this, the organisation of the relationship between men and women in society is also intended, and directing human beings towards high and lofty aims is intended. Men and women are commanded to make their sexual inclinations and desires subject to the Shari'ah. There is very lofty wisdom in this, and by adhering to this discipline a human being can perform his duties on this earth well.

Dhikr kathir (remembering Allah much): this is the quality through which a person's whole life becomes connected. The actions of life are connected to the worldview. Thus a person's heart is at all times conscious that Allah is watching. He holds firmly to Allah's rope and connection. No thought, no imagination and no action of his lies outside this connection. Then, through the remembrance of Allah, his heart is illuminated with divine light, pure and clean. The whole life of such a person is clean, pure and radiant.

Those in whom these qualities are gathered together form a personality that is a perfect personality, distinguished in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ (33:35). Thus these verses have enumerated here the fundamental elements of the personality of the Muslim man and the Muslim woman. This verse comes after the guidance that was given to the Prophet ﷺ at the beginning of this section. Here, women are mentioned especially along with men, in order to show that as Muslims and as human beings there is no difference between them, and that the Islamic status that men have in society is also that of women. In the Islamic worldview, faith, worship, morality and every aspect of conduct in life, there is no distinction between men and women.

**Lesson 191: At a Glance**

This lesson also aims to strengthen the ties between the Islamic society and the Islamic community. Its purpose is to abolish the custom of adoption (tabanni) in Islamic society and to establish relationships in the new Islamic society on their true principles. To abolish this custom, Allah began the practical implementation with the Prophet ﷺ himself. Among the Arabs, it was the custom that just as the wife of one's son was forbidden to a man, so too the divorced wife of an adopted son (mu'abbanā, adopted son) was considered forbidden to that man. In the Islamic society, for the divorced wife of an adopted son to be declared lawful, there had to be an example and a precedent. Without an example, merely making a law could not have brought about this change. Therefore Allah chose the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for this purpose, and this was as great a burden as the burden of prophethood. The reaction to this event proved that no one other than the Messenger of Allah could have broken this custom. This custom had very deep roots in society, and no one except the Prophet ﷺ could have done such an unusual and unfamiliar thing. For this reason, the lengthy commentary that comes after this event explains how the Muslims' relationship with God should be, how they should be with one another, and what attitude they should adopt towards the Prophet's duties. All these measures were taken for the ease of the people, and so that people would accept Allah's commands with submission and contentment, and with the joy of their hearts.

Before narrating this event, the principle is stated that it is obligatory for the Muslims to obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. When Allah and His Messenger ﷺ make a decision, the Muslims have no right to object in any such matter. This also shows that this custom had deep roots among the Arabs and could not easily be abolished. It was a severe custom.

**Lesson 191: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 36 to 48**

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ (33:36)

It is related in the narrations that this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with her). The Prophet ﷺ wished to break down the class distinctions that existed within the Muslim community, so that people would become equal, just as the teeth of a comb are equal. No one would have superiority over others except through piety. In that era, freed slaves were called mawālī, and these people were considered somewhat inferior to ordinary people. Zayd ibn Harithah, a freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was one of them. The Messenger of Allah had made him his adopted son (mu'abbanā). The Prophet ﷺ wanted to set the example of having a noble lady from the Banū Hāshim, who was also a close relative of the Prophet ﷺ, namely Zaynab bint Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with her), married to Zayd, so that this class distinction would be eliminated, and he would do this himself within his own family. It should be noted here that just as the custom of adoption was firm and strong, so too in society freed slaves were regarded as people of lower status. This distinction could also be eliminated only through the practical step of the Prophet ﷺ himself, so that the community would follow his example and all of humanity would proceed on one path.

Ibn Kathir, in his Tafsīr, cites a narration from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) through ʿAwfī that the occasion of revelation of the verse "Wa mā kāna..." is this: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to propose on behalf of Zayd ibn Harithah to a young woman, so he went to Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah. When he proposed to her, she said that she did not want to marry him. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Marry him." She then said that she would think it over. While this conversation was taking place, this verse was revealed:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair.﴾ (33:36)

Upon this, Zaynab said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you approve that I should marry him?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "Yes, I have indeed decided this." Then she said, "Very well, I accept this proposal. I will not disobey the Messenger of Allah. I have given myself to him in marriage."

Ibn Ṣuʿayh narrated from Abū ʿUmrah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed Zaynab bint Jahsh for Zayd ibn Harithah. She did not like it and said, "I am superior to him in lineage and status." She was a woman of harsh temperament. Upon this, this verse was revealed:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (33:36)

The same interpretation has been given by Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: that this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh, and it was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ proposed her for Zayd ibn Harithah. First she refused, and then she accepted.

Ibn Kathir, in his Tafsīr, also cites another narration: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says that this verse was revealed concerning Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. She was the first woman who migrated after the Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah. She had offered herself to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Very well, I accept." The Prophet ﷺ then gave her in marriage to Zayd ibn Harithah (perhaps after Zaynab's separation). Upon this, this woman and her brother became displeased. They said, "We had offered ourselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave her to his slave." Then this verse was revealed:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair.﴾ (33:36)

They say that the Qur'an contains an even more comprehensive command:

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.﴾ (33:6)

They said that the earlier verse is specific, and this one is comprehensive.

Imām Aḥmad narrated a third narration as well: through ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): the Prophet ﷺ sent a proposal for Julaybīb to the father of a woman from the Anṣār. That man said, "I will consult her mother." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Very well, consult her." The man went to his wife and mentioned it. The woman said, "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has found no one but Julaybīb! We have rejected the proposals of so-and-so and so-and-so." The young woman was listening from behind a curtain. The man set out towards the Prophet ﷺ intending to refuse in his presence. The young woman said, "Are you people rejecting the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ approves this for you, then accept it." In effect, she adopted an attitude superior to that of her parents. Both of them said, "She is right." So the man went to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "If you are pleased, we are pleased." The Prophet ﷺ said, "I am indeed pleased." It is said that he then gave the young woman in marriage to Julaybīb, who was a freed slave.

We have quoted this third narration, which concerns Julaybīb, here as well, because it relates to a campaign through which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to break the mentality of ancestral traditions, since Islam sought to establish social equality. The aim of this campaign was to build the Islamic society upon modern concepts. Regarding the values that Islam established for life in this earthly world, and in accordance with them, Islam had undertaken the task of freeing people from futile traditional bonds, and this campaign was connected with that spirit.

In any case, the wording of the verse is general beyond any particular event. It may relate to the abolition of the custom of adoption, and it may also mean that marriage to the divorced wife of an adopted son is permissible. It may also relate to the event in which the Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab after Zayd had divorced her. Upon this, a great uproar arose in Madinah, and even today some enemies of Islam use this as a basis for criticizing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They build layers of falsehood upon this very event. Whether the occasion of revelation is what is mentioned in these narrations, or the marriage of Zaynab bint Jahsh to the Prophet ﷺ, the principle is very general: once Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, the Muslims have no choice in that matter.

In short, among the basic elements of the Islamic worldview, this element was such that it had settled thoroughly in the hearts of the first Muslim community. Certainty of it had come into their hearts, and their consciousness was immersed in it. What was this element? It is that, after accepting Islam, nothing remains in their own control. They themselves, all their possessions, and their emotions are all in the control of Allah. He turns them however He wills, and their status is the same as that of this universe. They are a part of it, and Allah directs it as He wills, just as He directs the other things of this universe. In the running of this great existence, Allah has assigned them duties, and they obey them. The role that has been fixed for them on this grand stage, they will fully perform. They do not have the authority to determine a role for themselves, because they themselves are not more aware of the story they are to present. Moreover, they do not choose for themselves any movement or role of their own, for in that way the entire play of any drama would be ruined. They are not the director of this play. They are the actors, and they are obedient to the director. Their wages for their role are fixed. They should perform their role, and the rest is their wage; they have no right to object.

They have submitted before Allah. They have accepted all the components of the Islamic system. Therefore, after this covenant, nothing remains in their control, and just as this universe moves by the command of Allah, they too should move in accordance with the divine Sharia. In all their movements they should perform their fixed role, and move in their orbit as the planets move in their orbits: neither this way nor that, neither forward nor backward, in balance with all the other planets.

These people have submitted to all the events that the divine decree has destined for them. Their inner consciousness has accepted that whatever befalls them befalls by the command of Allah. For a person, every event and every state is sent by Allah, and he should accept Allah's decree joyfully and with complete tranquility. Gradually their condition became such that they did not wonder at the decisions of Allah when they descended upon them. They did not protect themselves through outward show and lamentation, nor did they feel pain and remain silent through patience and perseverance. Rather, their condition became such that they welcomed the decisions as if they had been forewarned and were awaiting them. The decision that was coming was already within their perception and consciousness. They knew it, and it was the voice of their conscience. No astonishment, no strangeness, and no aversion arose within them.

For this reason, they did not wish that the course of the heavens would speed up, so that the things they desired would happen quickly. Nor did they wish that certain events would occur sooner so that some of their needs might be fulfilled. They walked alongside the decree of Allah in their own manner, and wherever this decree brought them, they were content with it and rejoiced. What they had, they spent in that path. They sacrificed even their lives and spent their wealth. They neither hurried nor felt constricted, neither became proud nor felt regret. They were fully certain that whatever was happening was the decision of Allah; what Allah wills, happens, and every matter has an appointed time and a recorded term.

Their steps were taken in complete submission before Allah. Their movements were in accordance with Allah's direction. They possessed a full consciousness of security, trust, and certainty. They walked with the decree with great simplicity, gentleness, and ease.

The effect of this submission and contentment was not that they abstained from action, nor that they squandered everything they possessed, nor that they reduced effort and struggle because of their belief in the decree. They did not disregard the means. They did not take upon themselves things beyond their capacity, that is, what is beyond their power. Nor did they step outside the bounds of human nature and its limitations. They were weak, and they were also strong. They did not claim qualities that were not theirs. They did not like to be praised for an act they had not performed, nor did they claim acts they had not done.

They would submit absolutely before the decree of Allah, and then practically strive wherever they had the ability. They had established a beautiful balance in every matter, and they did what was within their capacity. In the conduct of the first community, this balance was entirely complete, and this balance was their distinctive feature. It was this balance that made them fit to bear that great trust, which the mountains had refused to bear.

The first community of Islam displayed these miracles in its life and made them a reality. These miracles were the result of that balance. These miracles occurred in that human society itself: the movements and deeds of that community were balanced in such a way that this community was organized like the celestial spheres and moved with harmony. Their measures and actions were like the orderly revolution of time. These people did not clash with nature, nor did they become entangled so that the turning of time would confuse them. Rather, they walked with the system of destiny and decree, of which the turning of time is a part. For this reason, they produced in an extremely short period results that history had not been able to produce.

This revolution took place because they moved in their actions along with the movement of this entire universe. They took their steps in accordance with the decree of Allah. It was this revolution that produced the miracles. These miracles were brought into being by the One who created the heavens and the earth, who created the stars and the spheres, and who brought the first generation to be content with the decree of Allah in the same way that the heavens cannot deviate even a hair's breadth from the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. This is the truth to which most of the verses of the Holy Qur'an point. Allah says:

﴿Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.﴾ And in another place:

﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills.﴾ In another place:

﴿Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah.﴾ This is guidance in its great reality and in its broad meaning, that is, the guidance as to what the station of man is in this great universe, and that his movement should harmonize with the movement of the universe. Human struggle cannot bear fruit until the heart of man is guided in this sense. The struggle of an individual cannot be in harmony with the movement of this universe. And as long as the human consciousness and conscience are not content with the decree of Allah, in the sense that whatever happens here happens by the will of Allah, [such struggle cannot bear fruit]. From this exposition it becomes clear that this verse of the Qur'an:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair...﴾ (33:36) is not restricted to a particular incident. It is a more general, comprehensive and complete principle, and it has far-reaching consequences. It is a fundamental constitutional principle of the Islamic system.

After this comes the matter of the Prophet ﷺ with Zaynab bint Jahsh.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 37–40:

وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ كَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا (37–40)

At the very beginning of this Surah, the custom of adoption (tabanni, adopting as a son) was abolished, and it was commanded that such adopted sons be attributed to their real fathers, and that family relationships be founded upon true lineage.

وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدْعِيَاءَكُمْ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا (33:4–5) "He has not made your adopted sons your real sons. These are merely words which you utter with your mouths. But Allah speaks the truth, and He guides to the right way. Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. And if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in faith and your companions. There is no blame upon you for what you do inadvertently, but there is blame for what your hearts intend. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

In Arab society, the customs of adopted sons were deeply rooted and had strong effects. Erasing these effects was not as easy as erasing the reality of adoption itself, because collective customs leave deep impressions on hearts. Therefore, to eliminate such customs, strict measures are needed in opposition to them. Generally, the first measures taken face outcry, and in the beginning they also have an effect on people's souls.

Earlier it was mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arranged the marriage of Zayd ibn Harithah. He was the adopted son of the Prophet ﷺ, and he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad. Afterwards he came to be called Zayd ibn Harithah. This marriage was arranged with Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was the cousin of the Prophet ﷺ on his father's side. The purpose was to remove the status by which slaves were considered second-class people in Arab society, and to put into practice the principle of nobility and honour that Allah has established.

إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ "Verily, the most honourable of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." This example was to be established in practice, so that it would be a real example. After this, the wisdom of Divine Will required that the responsibilities of prophethood be increased by this responsibility as well: that the Messenger ﷺ himself should set the example of marrying the divorced wife of an adopted son, so that the deep traces of the custom of adoption would also be erased, and the Messenger ﷺ would present this model before society. In these circumstances, no one else had the courage to undertake this task, even though the custom of adoption had already been abolished legally and by Shariah.

Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ through revelation that Zayd would soon divorce his wife, and that he would have to marry her. This was the requirement of Divine wisdom. In the meantime, relations between Zayd and Zaynab had become strained, and the signs indicated that this marriage could not continue.

Zayd repeatedly complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that his life with Zaynab was very troubled, and that he could no longer continue living with her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to propagate the Islamic worldview with great boldness and did not care about anyone in this regard. But in the matter of marrying Zaynab, he too was hesitant. In this matter he too feared facing the public, and he always said to Zayd, the one upon whom Allah had bestowed favour by making him Muslim, and who then came close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved, and this love was such that it was greater than all others without exception. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ showed him this kindness: he freed him, trained him, and loved him greatly. To Zayd, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say:

أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah" (33:37). In reality, the Messenger ﷺ wished to postpone this great matter, after the occurrence of which he would have had hesitation in facing the public, as Allah explicitly stated:

وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ أَن تَخْشَاهُ (33:37) "And you were concealing within yourself that which Allah was to bring to light; you were fearing the people, while Allah had more right that you fear Him." Allah had told the Prophet ﷺ the cause, that if Zayd divorced her, the Prophet ﷺ would have to marry her. This matter was not an explicit command; otherwise the Messenger ﷺ would not have hesitated in it, nor postponed it, nor tried to avoid it, and the Messenger ﷺ would have announced it at that time. Whatever the consequences might be, however, this matter was placed in the heart of the Prophet ﷺ by way of inspiration, and the Messenger ﷺ was anxious at that time that people would raise an uproar, until by the command of Allah Zayd divorced her. Neither Zayd nor Zaynab imagined that after this there would be a marriage with the Messenger ﷺ, because among the Arabs it was a legal custom that marriage with the divorced wife of an adopted son was not permissible. Even after the custom and law of adoption had been abolished, people still considered the divorced wife of an adopted son to be forbidden, and the command for her to be made lawful had not yet come. This event alone ended this custom, but this event was nonetheless a shock in that society and a unique and new matter.

Through this commentary, all those narrations are removed upon which the enemies of Islam, in both the ancient and modern periods, relied to compose fabrications and to make embellishments. The matter was simply this.

فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِّنْهَا وَطَرًا ۔۔۔۔۔ "So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there would be no difficulty for the believers regarding the wives of their adopted sons when they have accomplished their need from them" (33:37). This event was one of the heavy responsibilities of prophethood that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertook himself. Thus he set an example in eradicating a custom of Jahili society in a matter which in the days of ignorance was regarded as a detestable act. This act was considered so detestable that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not hesitated in great matters relating to the Islamic worldview, yet he had doubts in this one. For example, he openly denounced the self-invented deities of the Arabs, and he declared plainly that our forefathers were in error.

وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا "And the command of Allah must be carried out" (33:37). The marriage of Zaynab to the Messenger ﷺ had been settled after the completion of her waiting period. That is, it could not be rejected and there was no escape from it. This was a reality, and an inescapable reality, and no one could evade it.

The Prophet's ﷺ marriage to Zaynab took place after her waiting period had passed, and the Messenger ﷺ had sent the proposal to her through Zayd. Zayd was very dear to the Messenger ﷺ. He went and gave her the Messenger's ﷺ proposal.

It is narrated from Anas ؓ, who said: when Zaynab's waiting period ended, the Messenger ﷺ said to Zayd ibn Harithah, "Go and propose to Zaynab on my behalf." Zayd went; at that time she was mixing leaven into dough. He said that when he saw her, it became difficult for him to face her. He could not look at her, nor could he say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her. He turned his back to her, and while returning he said, "O Zaynab, good news for you! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to you so that I may convey his proposal to you." She said, "I will not do anything until I have consulted my Lord regarding this matter." She got up and began to pray at her place of prayer. Upon this, these verses were revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ afterwards came to her without seeking her permission. (Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim and Nasa'i through the route of Sulayman ibn Mughirah.)

In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated from Anas that Zaynab used to boast to the other wives of the Prophet ﷺ, "Your marriages were arranged by your relatives, but my marriage was arranged by Allah above the seven heavens."

This matter did not settle so easily; rather, in Islamic society it caused an upheaval, and the hypocrites found an issue: that the Messenger ﷺ had married the wife of his son. Since this matter concerned legal reform within Islamic society and it was necessary to establish a new principle for the Islamic society, Allah emphasized it further, and then removed the strangeness that people perceived in it, and returned matters to their true reality.

مَّا كَانَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيمَا فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ (33:38) "There is no difficulty upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him" (33:38). Allah had made it obligatory upon the Prophet that his marriage to Zaynab should take place, so that this Jahili custom would be broken, namely that no one could marry the wife of his adopted son when that son had divorced her or died. And that the Prophet ﷺ was not the first messenger; before him, such things had happened with other messengers.

سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ (33:38) "This is the way of Allah with those who passed before, and the command of Allah is a decree determined" (33:38). So this matter proceeds according to the Sunnah of Allah and there is no change or alteration in it. Similarly, Allah has been uprooting from its foundation those customs and traditions which have prevailed in society and which had no reality or benefit.

وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قَدَرًا مَّقْدُورًا (33:38) "And the command of Allah is a decree determined." The command of Allah is enforced, and it must be enforced. Nothing can stand as an obstacle before it, and nothing should. Allah settles all matters with great skill and with great wisdom, and behind them lie the purposes that are before Allah. It is Allah alone who knows the need for these commands and their importance in every time and place, and Allah has commanded His Messenger to erase this custom, to eradicate its practical traces as well, and to do this himself. No obstacle can be placed in the way of the implementation of Allah's command, and this has been the Sunnah of the Messengers of Allah, of all the messengers who passed:

الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسَالَاتِ اللَّهِ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ إِلَّا اللَّهَ (33:39) "Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none but Allah" (33:39). The way of such people is that they actually establish the system of Allah, and they do not fear the words of people. They perform their duties. They fear none but Allah. They convey the commands of Allah and enforce them.

وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا (33:39) "And Allah suffices as a reckoner" (33:39). Allah alone will take the account of good and evil, and people have no right to call their Prophet to account.

مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ (33:40) "Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men" (33:40). Therefore Zaynab is not the divorced wife of any son of Muhammad. Zayd ibn Muhammad is in reality Zayd ibn Harithah. Therefore there is nothing strange in this if it is viewed with a realistic outlook: the relationship of Muhammad ﷺ with all people is the relationship of a Prophet with his people; he is not the father of any of them.

وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ (33:40) "But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets" (33:40). This is why he ﷺ makes law. This is the everlasting and final Shariah, and it is to remain until the Day of Resurrection. After this, there will be no change or alteration in these laws.

وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا (33:40) "And Allah is Knowing of all things" (33:40). It is Allah alone who knows which law is beneficial for humanity. It is Allah who made it obligatory upon the Prophet to do this deed, and who appointed this ease for him, so that the restriction regarding the matter of adopted sons would be removed for people, when they have divorced a wife and have completed their need from her and have set her free. Allah has decided according to His knowledge, and it is Allah who legislates according to His wisdom and knowledge.

Now, in the context of the discourse, guidance is given to strengthen the relationship with Allah: remember Allah, morning and evening, and keep prostrating before Him. It is He who, by His kindness and mercy, brought you out of darkness into light. How merciful He is to the believers! When these believers appear on the Day of Resurrection, there will be greetings of blessing and peace from every side.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 37–40:

وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ كَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا (37–40)

At the very beginning of this Surah, the custom of adoption (tabanni, adopting as a son) was abolished, and it was commanded that such adopted sons be attributed to their real fathers, and that family relationships be founded upon true lineage.

وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدْعِيَاءَكُمْ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا (33:4–5) "He has not made your adopted sons your real sons. These are merely words which you utter with your mouths. But Allah speaks the truth, and He guides to the right way. Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. And if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in faith and your companions. There is no blame upon you for what you do inadvertently, but there is blame for what your hearts intend. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

In Arab society, the customs of adopted sons were deeply rooted and had strong effects. Erasing these effects was not as easy as erasing the reality of adoption itself, because collective customs leave deep impressions on hearts. Therefore, to eliminate such customs, strict measures are needed in opposition to them. Generally, the first measures taken face outcry, and in the beginning they also have an effect on people's souls.

Earlier it was mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arranged the marriage of Zayd ibn Harithah. He was the adopted son of the Prophet ﷺ, and he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad. Afterwards he came to be called Zayd ibn Harithah. This marriage was arranged with Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was the cousin of the Prophet ﷺ on his father's side. The purpose was to remove the status by which slaves were considered second-class people in Arab society, and to put into practice the principle of nobility and honour that Allah has established.

إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ "Verily, the most honourable of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." This example was to be established in practice, so that it would be a real example. After this, the wisdom of Divine Will required that the responsibilities of prophethood be increased by this responsibility as well: that the Messenger ﷺ himself should set the example of marrying the divorced wife of an adopted son, so that the deep traces of the custom of adoption would also be erased, and the Messenger ﷺ would present this model before society. In these circumstances, no one else had the courage to undertake this task, even though the custom of adoption had already been abolished legally and by Shariah.

Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ through revelation that Zayd would soon divorce his wife, and that he would have to marry her. This was the requirement of Divine wisdom. In the meantime, relations between Zayd and Zaynab had become strained, and the signs indicated that this marriage could not continue.

Zayd repeatedly complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that his life with Zaynab was very troubled, and that he could no longer continue living with her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to propagate the Islamic worldview with great boldness and did not care about anyone in this regard. But in the matter of marrying Zaynab, he too was hesitant. In this matter he too feared facing the public, and he always said to Zayd, the one upon whom Allah had bestowed favour by making him Muslim, and who then came close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved, and this love was such that it was greater than all others without exception. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ showed him this kindness: he freed him, trained him, and loved him greatly. To Zayd, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say:

أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah" (33:37). In reality, the Messenger ﷺ wished to postpone this great matter, after the occurrence of which he would have had hesitation in facing the public, as Allah explicitly stated:

وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ أَن تَخْشَاهُ (33:37) "And you were concealing within yourself that which Allah was to bring to light; you were fearing the people, while Allah had more right that you fear Him." Allah had told the Prophet ﷺ the cause, that if Zayd divorced her, the Prophet ﷺ would have to marry her. This matter was not an explicit command; otherwise the Messenger ﷺ would not have hesitated in it, nor postponed it, nor tried to avoid it, and the Messenger ﷺ would have announced it at that time. Whatever the consequences might be, however, this matter was placed in the heart of the Prophet ﷺ by way of inspiration, and the Messenger ﷺ was anxious at that time that people would raise an uproar, until by the command of Allah Zayd divorced her. Neither Zayd nor Zaynab imagined that after this there would be a marriage with the Messenger ﷺ, because among the Arabs it was a legal custom that marriage with the divorced wife of an adopted son was not permissible. Even after the custom and law of adoption had been abolished, people still considered the divorced wife of an adopted son to be forbidden, and the command for her to be made lawful had not yet come. This event alone ended this custom, but this event was nonetheless a shock in that society and a unique and new matter.

Through this commentary, all those narrations are removed upon which the enemies of Islam, in both the ancient and modern periods, relied to compose fabrications and to make embellishments. The matter was simply this.

فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِّنْهَا وَطَرًا ۔۔۔۔۔ "So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there would be no difficulty for the believers regarding the wives of their adopted sons when they have accomplished their need from them" (33:37). This event was one of the heavy responsibilities of prophethood that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertook himself. Thus he set an example in eradicating a custom of Jahili society in a matter which in the days of ignorance was regarded as a detestable act. This act was considered so detestable that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not hesitated in great matters relating to the Islamic worldview, yet he had doubts in this one. For example, he openly denounced the self-invented deities of the Arabs, and he declared plainly that our forefathers were in error.

وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا "And the command of Allah must be carried out" (33:37). The marriage of Zaynab to the Messenger ﷺ had been settled after the completion of her waiting period. That is, it could not be rejected and there was no escape from it. This was a reality, and an inescapable reality, and no one could evade it.

The Prophet's ﷺ marriage to Zaynab took place after her waiting period had passed, and the Messenger ﷺ had sent the proposal to her through Zayd. Zayd was very dear to the Messenger ﷺ. He went and gave her the Messenger's ﷺ proposal.

It is narrated from Anas ؓ, who said: when Zaynab's waiting period ended, the Messenger ﷺ said to Zayd ibn Harithah, "Go and propose to Zaynab on my behalf." Zayd went; at that time she was mixing leaven into dough. He said that when he saw her, it became difficult for him to face her. He could not look at her, nor could he say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her. He turned his back to her, and while returning he said, "O Zaynab, good news for you! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to you so that I may convey his proposal to you." She said, "I will not do anything until I have consulted my Lord regarding this matter." She got up and began to pray at her place of prayer. Upon this, these verses were revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ afterwards came to her without seeking her permission. (Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim and Nasa'i through the route of Sulayman ibn Mughirah.)

In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated from Anas that Zaynab used to boast to the other wives of the Prophet ﷺ, "Your marriages were arranged by your relatives, but my marriage was arranged by Allah above the seven heavens."

This matter did not settle so easily; rather, in Islamic society it caused an upheaval, and the hypocrites found an issue: that the Messenger ﷺ had married the wife of his son. Since this matter concerned legal reform within Islamic society and it was necessary to establish a new principle for the Islamic society, Allah emphasized it further, and then removed the strangeness that people perceived in it, and returned matters to their true reality.

مَّا كَانَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيمَا فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ (33:38) "There is no difficulty upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him" (33:38). And that the Prophet ﷺ was not the first messenger; before him, such things had happened with other messengers.

سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ (33:38) "This is the way of Allah with those who passed before, and the command of Allah is a decree determined" (33:38). So this matter proceeds according to the Sunnah of Allah and there is no change or alteration in it. Similarly, Allah has been uprooting from its foundation those customs and traditions which have prevailed in society and which had no reality or benefit.

وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قَدَرًا مَّقْدُورًا (33:38) "And the command of Allah is a decree determined." The command of Allah is enforced, and it must be enforced. Nothing can stand as an obstacle before it, and nothing should. Allah settles all matters with great skill and with great wisdom, and behind them lie the purposes that are before Allah. It is Allah alone who knows the need for these commands and their importance in every time and place, and Allah has commanded His Messenger to erase this custom, to eradicate its practical traces as well, and to do this himself. No obstacle can be placed in the way of the implementation of Allah's command, and this has been the Sunnah of the Messengers of Allah, of all the messengers who passed:

الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسَالَاتِ اللَّهِ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ إِلَّا اللَّهَ (33:39) "Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none but Allah" (33:39). The way of such people is that they actually establish the system of Allah, and they do not fear the words of people. They perform their duties. They fear none but Allah. They convey the commands of Allah and enforce them.

وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا (33:39) "And Allah suffices as a reckoner" (33:39). Allah alone will take the account of good and evil, and people have no right to call their Prophet to account.

مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ (33:40) "Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men" (33:40). Therefore Zaynab is not the divorced wife of any son of Muhammad. Zayd ibn Muhammad is in reality Zayd ibn Harithah. Therefore there is nothing strange in this if it is viewed with a realistic outlook: the relationship of Muhammad ﷺ with all people is the relationship of a Prophet with his people; he is not the father of any of them.

وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ (33:40) "But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets" (33:40). This is why he ﷺ makes law. When these believers appear on the Day of Resurrection, there will be greetings of blessing and peace from every side.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah al-Ahzab, verses 41–44**

﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ (33:41–44)

Remembrance of Allah (*dhikr*, the remembrance of God) keeps a person connected to Allah, and the heart stays occupied with the thought that Allah alone is the One who does everything. Mere repetition of Allah's name with the tongue is not the whole of *dhikr*. Establishing the *salah* (ritual prayer) is also a form of *dhikr*. In fact, in the Qur'an and Sunnah, *dhikr* almost always means *salah*. Imam Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated, through al-A'mash, that he related from al-Aghar, Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a man wakes his wife at night and both of them pray two *rak'ahs*, they will both be counted among the men and women who remember Allah much."

Although *dhikr* of Allah is broader than *salah*, every situation in which a servant remembers Allah is *dhikr* of Allah, in which the servant's heart is connected to the Lord, whether or not he utters it with his tongue. The essential matter is that a person becomes connected to Allah in heart and spirit. When a person is heedless of Allah, his heart is empty, he is careless, and he is bewildered and distressed. When he reaches Allah and remembers Him, he becomes content and at peace. Now his heart is full. He becomes serious. He finds tranquillity and rest. He comes to know the path of life, and he is aware of his *minhaj* (way or method). He knows where he is, where he has to go, and what his path is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 45–48:

Yā ayyuhan-Nabiyyu innā arsalnāka... wa kafā billāhi wakīlā (33:45–48)

It is the prescribed duty of the Prophet that he be a witness over the people. Therefore, people should conduct themselves in such a way that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is able to give a good testimony, since he is to give a true testimony. He is to make no alteration or change to the actual event. The Messenger is a bearer of glad tidings to those who do good deeds. For righteous people, the mercy of Allah awaits, and he is a warner to the heedless and misguided people that a severe punishment awaits them, so that these unfortunate ones do not perish in heedlessness; and if punishment is inflicted, it is after the warning.

Wa dā'iyan ilallāh (33:46) "and as one who calls to Allah." He was not sent merely so that you might have a good worldly life, so that you become dominant in the world and your national honour is exalted. He was not appointed as a caller for tribal partisanship (jāhiliyyah 'aṣabiyyāt), nor was he raised up for the acquisition of war booty. The establishment of a system of government is not the objective. Calling to Allah alone is their manifesto and objective, and they began this work by the command of Allah. It is neither from themselves nor voluntary. Nor do you undertake this work as a volunteer on your own initiative. All of this work is by the command of Allah.

Wa sirājan munīrā (33:46) "and as a illuminating lamp." You dispel darkness. You establish testimony. You define the path and you are for people such a guide as a shining lamp is. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came bringing this light in this manner. This light was a clear conception, a clear ideology and belief, which illuminated the entire universe. It clarified the connection between this universe and man, and defined the position and rank of man in this universe. It explained the values upon which this universe is established. It defined the purpose of man, his aim, and the method of attaining it, in a most clear style and in a most natural manner, such that the message descends to the depths of the human heart. The most difficult problems and the most complicated issues in the ups and downs of life have been resolved by the simplest of methods. It is again explained in detail that the responsibilities of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ include the addition that he is a bearer of glad tidings to the believers.

Wa bashshiril-mu'minīna bi'anna lahum minallāhi fadlan kabīrā (33:47) "And give glad tidings to those who believe that for them is a great bounty from Allah." Earlier, the verse "Yā ayyuhan-Nabiyyu innā arsalnāka shāhidan wa mubashshiran wa nadhīrā (33:45)" [O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner] had described him as a bearer of glad tidings in summary, and this detail is given so that the believers may be certain that a great bounty and favour of Allah will be upon them, and that the laws and regulations being prepared for them, and the path and practice that the Prophet is laying down by his own conduct, will ultimately be glad tidings and the good news of a great bounty and favour for them.

In this address, the Prophet ﷺ is forbidden from obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites in any matter, and from paying any heed to the harm these people inflict upon him and the believers. He should rely upon Allah alone. He alone is sufficient as a helper for you.

Wa lā tuṭiʿil-kāfirīna wal-munāfiqīna... wa kafā billāhi wakīlā (33:48) "And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and put your trust in Allah; Allah is sufficient as a Trustee for one who entrusts his affairs to Him." This is the same address that was at the beginning of the surah, before legislation was begun there and modern administrative instructions were given. Here, however, there is an additional point: O Prophet, do not heed the harm inflicted by the disbelievers and hypocrites, do not follow them in any matter, and do not rely on them in any matter, because Allah alone is worthy of trust.

Wa kafā billāhi wakīlā (33:48) "Allah is sufficient for one who entrusts his affairs to Him."

Thus, the introduction and commentary regarding the incident of Zayd and Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her) and the permissibility of marriage to the wives of adopted sons are both lengthy, and this practical example, which the Prophet ﷺ himself found very heavy to convey, required explanation from Allah and encouragement for the people. In these matters, it was necessary to strengthen one's connection with Allah, so that the servant gains a deep awareness of Allah's favour and mercy, and receives these commands with cheerfulness, accepts them, and acts upon them with submission and contentment.

Yā ayyuhan-Nabiyyu innā arsalnāka... wa kafā billāhi wakīlā (33:45–48)

It is the prescribed duty of the Prophet that he be a witness over the people. Therefore, people should conduct themselves in such a way that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is able to give a good testimony, since he is to give a true testimony. He is to make no alteration or change to the actual event. The Messenger is a bearer of glad tidings to those who do good deeds. For righteous people, the mercy of Allah awaits, and he is a warner to the heedless and misguided people that a severe punishment awaits them, so that these unfortunate ones do not perish in heedlessness; and if punishment is inflicted, it is after the warning.

Wa dā'iyan ilallāh (33:46) "and as one who calls to Allah." He was not sent merely so that you might have a good worldly life, so that you become dominant in the world and your national honour is exalted. He was not appointed as a caller for tribal partisanship (jāhiliyyah 'aṣabiyyāt), nor was he raised up for the acquisition of war booty. The establishment of a system of government is not the objective. Calling to Allah alone is their manifesto and objective, and they began this work by the command of Allah. It is neither from themselves nor voluntary. Nor do you undertake this work as a volunteer on your own initiative. All of this work is by the command of Allah.

Wa sirājan munīrā (33:46) "and as a illuminating lamp." You dispel darkness. You establish testimony. You define the path and you are for people such a guide as a shining lamp is. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came bringing this light in this manner. This light was a clear conception, a clear ideology and belief, which illuminated the entire universe. It clarified the connection between this universe and man, and defined the position and rank of man in this universe. It explained the values upon which this universe is established. It defined the purpose of man, his aim, and the method of attaining it, in a most clear style and in a most natural manner, such that the message descends to the depths of the human heart. The most difficult problems and the most complicated issues in the ups and downs of life have been resolved by the simplest of methods. It is again explained in detail that the responsibilities of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ include the addition that he is a bearer of glad tidings to the believers.

Wa bashshiril-mu'minīna bi'anna lahum minallāhi fadlan kabīrā (33:47) "And give glad tidings to those who believe that for them is a great bounty from Allah." Earlier, the verse "Yā ayyuhan-Nabiyyu innā arsalnāka shāhidan wa mubashshiran wa nadhīrā (33:45)" [O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner] had described him as a bearer of glad tidings in summary, and this detail is given so that the believers may be certain that a great bounty and favour of Allah will be upon them, and that the laws and regulations being prepared for them, and the path and practice that the Prophet is laying down by his own conduct, will ultimately be glad tidings and the good news of a great bounty and favour for them.

In this address, the Prophet ﷺ is forbidden from obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites in any matter, and from paying any heed to the harm these people inflict upon him and the believers. He should rely upon Allah alone. He alone is sufficient as a helper for you.

Wa lā tuṭiʿil-kāfirīna wal-munāfiqīna... wa kafā billāhi wakīlā (33:48) "And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and put your trust in Allah; Allah is sufficient as a Trustee for one who entrusts his affairs to Him." This is the same address that was at the beginning of the surah, before legislation was begun there and modern administrative instructions were given. Here, however, there is an additional point: O Prophet, do not heed the harm inflicted by the disbelievers and hypocrites, do not follow them in any matter, and do not rely on them in any matter, because Allah alone is worthy of trust.

Wa kafā billāhi wakīlā (33:48) "Allah is sufficient for one who entrusts his affairs to Him."

Thus, the introduction and commentary regarding the incident of Zayd and Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her) and the permissibility of marriage to the wives of adopted sons are both lengthy, and this practical example, which the Prophet ﷺ himself found very heavy to convey, required explanation from Allah and encouragement for the people. In these matters, it was necessary to strengthen one's connection with Allah, so that the servant gains a deep awareness of Allah's favour and mercy, and receives these commands with cheerfulness, accepts them, and acts upon them with submission and contentment.
