Lesson No. 192: A Glance

The opening part of this lesson deals with general family and marital legislation: the ruling on a divorced woman whose divorce took place before consummation, her waiting period (iddah) and related matters. After this come the instructions for the family life of the Messenger ﷺ, his relations with his wives, the regulation of his contact with people outside, and the Muslims' connection with the household of the Messenger, followed by blessings and peace upon that household. Then comes the general command of hijab, which includes the daughters of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his wives and all the women of the believers: that when they go out for the call of nature, they should let their outer garments hang down over their chests, so that they may be recognised by that dress and not be molested. This was because hypocrites, wicked and immoral people, and dissolute men who spread rumours in Madinah, used to harass women. At the end, such people are warned that if they do not desist from these actions, severe measures will be taken against them.

All these legal, social and public-order measures were taken so that the society of Madinah might be organised fully along Islamic lines. The instructions concerning the household of the Prophet ﷺ are there because Allah wished to keep this household as an open book for the generations to come until the Day of Resurrection, since this Book was to be read until the Day of Resurrection. Moreover, the recording of these instructions in the Divine Book was an honour for that household: Allah Himself was training it and making it an example until the Day of Resurrection.

Lesson No. 192: Explanation of the Verses

49 ... to ... 62

﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no waiting period for them to count. So provide for them and release them graciously.﴾ (33:49)

The rulings concerning a woman who has been divorced before consummation were mentioned earlier in Surah al-Baqarah:

﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not yet touched them or specified for them an obligation. But provide for them, the wealthy according to his capacity and the poor according to his capacity, a provision according to what is reasonable, an obligation upon the doers of good. And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then give half of what you specified, unless they forgo or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes. And to forgo is nearer to righteousness. And do not forget bounty among yourselves. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (2:237-238)

For a divorced woman who has not been consummated: if a dower has been fixed, half of it must be paid; and if no dower was fixed, she must nevertheless be given something, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his circumstances. In this verse, the matter of the waiting period is added, which was not there. The decision is that since there has been no consummation, there is no waiting period, because where there has been no intercourse between them, there is no question of purifying the womb through a waiting period, since no traces of the previous marriage exist, so that lineage is not confused and a child is not attributed to a man who is not really his, or so that a man does not lose a child that is his. But where there has been no consummation, the womb is clean. Therefore there is neither a waiting period nor any need to wait.

﴿So you have no right to demand from them any waiting period that you could count.﴾ "Provide for them" means give them some wealth: if a dower was fixed, half of it; and if none was fixed, still give something according to your financial means.

"And release them graciously" (33:49): neither keep them hanging, nor harm them, nor harbour resentment, nor prevent them from entering a new married life. This is a general command in this Surah, and it is for the whole Islamic society.

After this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is told which women have been made lawful for him, and the particular privileges of his person and of his household. These rulings came after the verse of Surah an-Nisa (﴿two, three or four﴾), where it had been made unlawful for Muslims to have more than four wives.

The Prophet ﷺ had nine wives in his household. Each marriage took place for a specific need. Aisha and Hafsah (may Allah be pleased with them) were the daughters of Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them), who were his closest companions. Umm Habibah was the daughter of Abu Sufyan. Umm Salamah, Sawdah bint Zam'ah and Zaynab bint Khuzaymah were among those who had been deprived of their husbands, and the Messenger ﷺ encouraged and honoured them. The story of Zaynab bint Jahsh has already passed: since she had been married, at the insistence of the Prophet ﷺ, to Zayd ibn Harithah, a freed slave, and that marriage did not succeed, Allah had her married to the Messenger ﷺ. Details have already been given of how this was done to console her and to remove the vestiges of the custom of adoption. Juwayriyah bint al-Harith of Banu al-Mustaliq and Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab both came as captives, and the Messenger ﷺ freed them and took them in marriage, so that ties might be established with those tribes, and so that these two daughters of chieftains might be honoured. Both had embraced Islam, although their peoples had been treated harshly.

All these women attained the status of the Mothers of the Believers, and when the verse of choice was revealed, they all chose Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and preferred the Hereafter to this world. Furthermore, when the number of wives was limited to four, it was difficult for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to accept this for the Messenger, peace be upon him. Allah showed them favour: He exempted the Messenger ﷺ from the verse of Surah al-Baqarah, and gave permission for him to keep all those women. All of them were made lawful for him, but then the command was also given that he could not add to them, nor could he exchange any one of them for another. This permission is restricted to the existing wives, so that they would not be deprived of the honour of being wives of the Messenger ﷺ, since previously they had already preferred Allah's Messenger and the abode of the Hereafter.

These are the subjects of these verses.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 50–52:

Ya ayyuha al-Nabi inna ahlalna ... ala kulli shay'in raqiba (50–52)

In this verse, the women mentioned were made lawful for the Prophet ﷺ, even though they exceeded the number of four, whereas for other Muslims more than four wives is forbidden. These categories are: the wives whom you married by giving them their mahr (bridal gift); the women who came into your possession as slaves (ma malakat yamin); the daughters of your paternal uncles and maternal aunts; the daughters of your paternal aunts and maternal uncles, but only those who migrated with you (hijrah). This is in honour of those women emigrants (muhajirat). Also, a woman who gives herself to the Prophet ﷺ without mahr, if the Prophet wishes to marry her. (There is disagreement in the narrations about whether the Messenger ﷺ actually married any woman of this category. The preferred view is that when women offered themselves to the Messenger ﷺ, he did marry them.) These categories were permitted for the Prophet ﷺ as a special privilege, because the Prophet ﷺ was also the guardian (wali) of the believing men and women. As for other people, they were bound by the laws Allah had prescribed concerning their wives and slave-women. This exception was made so that the Prophet ﷺ would not be afflicted with difficulties arising from his personal and communal circumstances.

After this, the Messenger ﷺ was also given the choice that if anyone offered herself to him, he could take her into his household or defer her. And for those whose matter he had deferred, he could later bring them into his household. He was also given the choice to bring back again those whom he had set aside.

Dhalika adna an ... bima ataytahunna kulluhunna (33:51): "This is more likely to keep their eyes cool and prevent them from grief, and they will all be pleased with whatever you give them." Thus this permission was granted under the particular circumstances of the Messenger ﷺ, because all the women were inclined towards him and desired contact with him. Allah had the most complete knowledge of these circumstances.

Wallahu ya'lamu ... aliman halima (33:51): "Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing."

After this comes the command that the women in the Prophet's household are lawful to him personally. Their number is not what is sought. Therefore, he may not bring in another woman in place of any of them. It is not known whether the Prophet ﷺ had added any woman before the revelation of this verse.

La yahillu laka al-nisa'u ... a'jabaka husnuhunna (33:52): "After this, other women are not lawful to you, nor is it permitted that you replace them with other wives, even though their beauty may please you greatly. There is no exception in this."

Illa ma malakat yaminuka (33:52): "Except for the slave-women, who are permitted to you." You may keep as many slave-women as you wish.

Wa kana Allahu ala kulli shay'in raqiba (33:52): "And Allah is Watchful over everything." It is related from Hadrat Aisha (RA) that this prohibition was also lifted before the death of the Messenger ﷺ, but despite the permission, the Messenger ﷺ did not marry any woman other than these, so they remained the Mothers of the Believers.

After this, the relations between the household of the Prophet ﷺ and the general Muslims are regulated: how people's connection with his wives will be during his lifetime, and what relationship will exist after his death. These commands came in accordance with the actual circumstances of that time, because some hypocrites and some people of diseased character used to cause distress to the Prophet ﷺ regarding his wives. Therefore, in these verses a severe warning is given to them, and it is stated that their conduct is extremely abominable in the sight of Allah. They may be hidden from people, but they cannot be hidden from Allah. Allah knows their mischief as well as their intentions.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 53:

Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū ... Allāha kāna bi-kulli shay'in ʿalīmā (33:53–54). Imam al-Bukhari relates the narration of Hadrat Anas ibn Malik that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he gave a feast of bread and meat, and I was sent to invite people. People would come, eat, and leave. I invited everyone until no one remained. Then I said, "O Messenger of Allah, no one is left." The Messenger ﷺ said, "Now lift the food-cloth." Three men remained seated in the room, talking. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and went to the room of Hadrat ʿĀʾishah ؓ and said, "As-salāmu ʿalaykum, O People of the House, wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh." She replied, "Wa ʿalaykumu s-salām wa raḥmatullāh." He asked, "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, how is your new wife? May Allah bless her for you." He ﷺ went to his other wives and spoke the same words as he had with ʿĀʾishah ؓ, and all of them gave the same reply. When the Messenger ﷺ returned, those three persons were still sitting as before. The Messenger ﷺ was extremely modest, so he went back to the room of Hadrat ʿĀʾishah ؓ. I do not know whether ʿĀʾishah ؓ informed the Messenger ﷺ that the people had left, or someone else informed him. When the Messenger ﷺ returned and placed one foot inside the threshold of the door while the other was still outside, he drew a curtain between me and himself, and at that time the verse of hijab was revealed.

This verse contains the etiquette that was absent in the Age of Ignorance, and which was even absent in the house of the Messenger ﷺ. People would enter houses without permission, as the details have passed in the explanation of the verse of seeking permission in Surah al-Nur. In the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ these etiquettes were not observed at all, because his house was a gathering place where people sat at all times to acquire knowledge and wisdom. Some would come, see that something was being cooked, and sit down so as to eat without an invitation. Some would remain sitting even after they had eaten, whether they had been invited or had entered on their own. Then they would become engrossed in conversation, not realising how much discomfort this caused the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some narrations report that while these three persons were talking, the Messenger ﷺ's bride was sitting in the same room, her face turned toward the wall, and the Messenger ﷺ felt shy about telling these people (that she was there), lest they be embarrassed, and so he did not say so. Then Allah made this announcement on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

Wa Allāha lā yastaḥyī min al-ḥaqq (33:53): "Allah is not ashamed to state the truth."

Narrations report that Hadrat ʿUmar ؓ, on account of his zeal and his sensitivity, used to propose before the Messenger ﷺ that the hijab be enforced, and he would also wish for it, until the verse of hijab was revealed. In a narration of Bukhari it is recorded that Hadrat ʿUmar ؓ said, "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, both the good and the bad come to you. Would that you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab."

In this verse it is taught that people should not enter the house of the Prophet without permission. When they are invited to a meal, they should enter; if they have not been invited, they should not come in haste, nor wait for the food to be cooked in the place of the feast. Then, when they have been served food, they should leave, and after eating they should not sit down merely for idle chat. Compared with the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Muslims today are more in need of these etiquettes, because even in this age of progress we are far from these etiquettes: those who are invited to a meal remain seated even after eating, indeed they hold lengthy talks while eating, and the household, who observe only some of the rules of hijab in Islam, are confined, while the guests are absorbed in their own talk. The truth is that Islamic etiquettes are beneficial for every age and every society, but what is needed is that we be ready to adopt Islamic and divine etiquettes. After this, the matter of hijab between the Prophet's ﷺ family and ordinary people comes forward.

Wa idhā sa'altumūhunna ... ḥijāb (33:53): "When you ask the wives of the Prophet for something, ask them from behind a screen." This hijab is purer for your hearts.

Dhalikum aṭhharu li-qulūbikum wa qulūbihinna (33:53): "That is a more proper way for the purity of your hearts and theirs." Therefore it is not permissible for anyone to say anything other than what Allah has said. Hence no one should say that mixing, unveiling, unrestrained talk, unrestricted meetings, companionship, and co-mingling of the sexes purify the hearts, and that in this way consciences become more chaste. Thus inclinations and desires are suppressed, and human conduct and consciousness become transparent. These are some of the nonsense that the fallen people among Allah's creation utter. I would advise that no one should speak in this way, when Allah says:

Wa idhā sa'altumūhunna matā'an ... qulūbihinna (33:53): "When you ask the wives of the Prophet for something, ask from behind a screen; this is a most proper way for the purity of your hearts and theirs." This is being said about the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, who are the Mothers of the Believers, and it is being said to those people who are the salt of the earth, the Companions of the Messenger, whose equal no one can even imagine. When Allah speaks, and from the other side a creature of Allah speaks, the word is Allah's, and the words of others are nonsense. To give weight to human words in preference to Allah's, only a person who holds the belief that a human being knows more than Allah could do so.

The experience of years has proven that what Allah said was truer, and the words of these small and dwarfish people have been proven wrong by the experiences of years and centuries. Today in the West, where the mixing of men and women has reached its extremes, have the hearts of all people become pure and clean? America is at the peak in this field. Just study the conditions of that country.

This verse shows that arriving even before being invited, waiting for the food to be cooked, and then, after finishing the meal, engaging in far-fetched talk was distressing to the Prophet ﷺ, and he remained silent out of modesty. Yet it does not befit Muslims to cause the Prophet ﷺ distress, or to marry his wives after him, since they are like their mothers. It is the requirement of the rank and station of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that after him no one should marry them, in order to uphold the sanctity and honour of that household.

Wa mā kāna lakum ... ba'dahu abadā (33:53): "It is not permissible for you to cause distress to the Messenger of Allah, nor that you marry his wives after him." Some narrations report that some hypocrites used to say that they were waiting for the Messenger ﷺ to die so that they might marry ʿĀʾishah ؓ.

Inna dhālikum kāna ʿinda Allāhi ʿaẓīmā (33:53): "Indeed, that is a grave sin in the sight of Allah." And how dreadful must be a sin that is grave in the sight of Allah. Not only this, but after it a further threat is given, which is very severe.

Ayat (33:54): "Whether you reveal a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things."

So the whole matter rests in Allah's hands. He is the Knower of everything apparent and hidden, He knows every plan and every thought, and this matter is, in His sight, a grave sin. If anyone still disputes with Him over it, then he is waging war against Allah, and whoever wages war against Allah will be destroyed. After this general veil, the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) have been permitted not to observe the veil before certain categories of mahram relatives, so that they may appear before them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 55:

لاجناح علیھن ۔۔۔۔۔ کل شئ شھیدا (55) ” “۔

These are the mahram relatives in whose presence all Muslim women are permitted to not observe hijab. It is not known which of these two verses was revealed first: this verse, which is specific to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), or the general verse of Surah al-Nur that applies to all Muslim women. The preferred view is that the command first came for the Mothers of the Believers (azwaj mutahharat) and then for all Muslim women, and this is in keeping with the nature of Allah's imposing obligations.

This permission is also linked with the fear of Allah. "Fear Allah; indeed Allah is aware of everything." Being mindful of taqwa (God-consciousness) and of Allah's watchfulness is generally the safeguard in such places, because taqwa is the final guarantee against every evil. This is the watchful Overseer who constantly observes the heart and mind.

The context moves a little further in warning people that they should not cause harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), neither regarding his person nor regarding his family. The vileness of this act is explained more clearly, and this is stated in two ways. The first way adopted is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is praised, and it is shown how exalted a station the Prophet (ﷺ) holds with Allah. The second way is that it is directly stated that those who harm the Messenger (ﷺ) in fact harm Allah, and the punishment for them with Allah is that they are removed from Allah's mercy, and they will be deprived in this world and the Hereafter, and this punishment will be inflicted upon them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 56–57:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...﴾ ... ﴿and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ (56–57)

The sending of blessings (ṣalāh) upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by Allah means that the Prophet is praised in the higher realm, and the blessings of the angels mean that they supplicate for the Prophet ﷺ. How great is the rank of the Messenger ﷺ with Allah, that the entire universe supplicates for him! Through this, the entire universe is illuminated, and it is a praise and commendation from Allah. It is that which remains, which is eternal and everlasting, and the entire universe keeps pace with it. What greater blessing and honour could there be than this? What comparison is there between the blessings and salutations of us human beings and the blessings and salutations of Allah and the entire universe? The demand that humans send blessings and salutations is made so that their humble voice too may join the echo of the universe and take part in this great praise, and in this way humans too may become claimants to participation in this great gathering, whereas the blessings and salutations from Allah will be eternal and everlasting.

Considering this great praise and glorification, in which the Lord, the angels, the universe and humans also take part: if some wretched person harms the Prophet ﷺ, who is the praised one of the universe, and the Lord of the universe, how abominable, how vile and how blameworthy does this act become!

﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah...﴾ ... ﴿and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ (33:57) "Those who harm Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment." This act becomes even more vile, that a creature harms its Creator. Yet people cannot harm Allah at all. Rather, the manner of the speech indicates that they inflict upon the Messenger of Allah such severe harm that it is as if harm reaches Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He. Therefore, their conduct is very bad, very vile and extremely abominable. After this, the mention of the harm to the believing men and women follows: harming them, slandering them by attributing to them that they have some fault, as these hypocrites ascribe things to them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 58:

﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women, without their having earned it, have certainly borne the slander and a clear sin.﴾ (33:58)

This shows that at that time there was a class in Madinah which was engaged in the pastime of harming the believing men and women in this manner. Evil things were attributed to the believers day and night. They plotted against them and fabricated accusations, just as this has always happened against Islamic movements in every era and every place. In every society of wicked and mischievous people, the believing men and women have always been treated in this same way. This is always the occupation of people with a diseased heart and of the hypocrites. Here Allah has taken upon Himself the defence of the believing women and has declared that their enemies are liars and people of Hell, and who could be more truthful than Allah?

After this, the command is given: ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments close around themselves﴾ (33:59). That is, when they go out they should let their outer garments (ajlabib, sing. jilbab) fall over their chests, so that they are recognised as respectable women. In such a way that their heads, faces and chests are covered. Juyub (﴿جيوب﴾) is the plural of jayb (جيب), and this is the open slit in a shirt or garment that is located on the chest. In that period, people used to harass women. Therefore, by such a dress these mischief-makers will be somewhat intimidated and will understand that these women are modest and chaste, and so they will not dare to attempt molestation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 59:

﴿یَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزْوَاجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَاءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَن يُعْرَفْنَ فَلَا يُؤْذَيْنَ ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا﴾ (59) ""

Suddi (Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi) says that there were debauched people in Madinah who, at that time, would go out at night, when the darkness had grown deep, and harass women in the narrow lanes of Madinah. This was because people's houses were small and women had to go outside for the call of nature. These debauchees would pursue the women. When they saw that a woman was wearing the hijab, they would say that she is a free woman, and so they would refrain from her. And when they saw that she had no veil, they would pounce upon her.

Mujahid says that the meaning is that they should draw the jilbab over themselves, so that it becomes known that these are free women, so that no debauchee harasses them or casts doubt upon them, and that...

﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا﴾ (33:59) "And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." That is, whatever occurred in the age of ignorance (jahiliyyah), Allah will overlook it, because at that time they had neither this command nor this knowledge. Thus we see that Islam was gradually purifying the corrupt society of Arabia, closing off every avenue of sedition, corruption and sexual licentiousness, and narrowing the circle of evil, so that the pure way and practice of Islam might gradually take root in the Islamic society.

Finally, these undesirable elements of Madinah are threatened: if the hypocrites, those of diseased morals, and those who spread inflammatory rumours do not desist, and do not abandon the activities in which they are engaged, then the Messenger of Allah will be commanded to take severe action against them. The Prophet, the believing men and the believing women will be set upon them, just as the Prophet and the Muslims gained complete authority over the Jews. Then it will become difficult for them to remain in Madinah, and they too will be expelled from the country. The action against them will be that those who cause harm to the believing men and believing women are liable to be killed, and wherever they are found their heads shall be severed, just as the fate of the Jews was witnessed by them, and just as in past ages the fate of non-Jewish debauchers and wrongdoers was always at the hands of the Prophets.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 60–62:

"Lā-in lam yantahi al-munāfiqūn..." to "Sunnat Allāh tabdīlā" (60–62)

This warning shows that after the elimination of the Banu Qurayza, the Muslims in Madinah had become a dominant power, the Islamic state was enforcing its moral teachings with strength, and the hypocrites (munafiqun) had become ineffective. They could only carry out secret conspiracies; they could not openly show themselves against the Muslims, and outwardly they appeared fearful and cowed.

Lesson No. 193: At a Glance

This is the last lesson of this Surah. In it, a response is given to the question that people used to ask about the Hour, and the demands they made for the Hour to be established. In reality, they doubted that the Hour would come. The answer given is that the matter of the establishment of the Hour is in Allah's hands. Its time is, however, far off, and it is possible that it may come upon you suddenly while you remain immersed in heedlessness. After this, from among the scenes of the Resurrection, one scene is presented which is by no means pleasing to those who demand the coming of the Hour. When their faces will be turned over in the Fire, and at that time they will be deeply remorseful for their disobedience to Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they will ask for double punishment for their leaders and their chieftains. This is such a shameful scene

that no one who is hasty for it would ever like it.

Now, bringing them back from that scene into this world, the example of the people of Musa (Moses) is again placed before them: that people also caused distress to Musa (peace be upon him), and then Allah cleared Musa of the accusation they had levelled against him. It appears that this was a practical incident. The allusion is as follows: those in Madinah who speak against the Messenger (ﷺ), saying that the Messenger (ﷺ) acted against the customs of the Arabs by marrying Zaynab, made a similar accusation against Musa as well. And the believers are told that in any matter they should speak plainly, and should not level accusations through allusion and innuendo, so that Allah may set right your deeds and conduct, forgive your sins, and that whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) will be granted by Allah a great success.

The Surah concludes with a magnificent observation: the heavens and the earth refused to bear the trust of the call of the Qur'an, but man accepted this great responsibility, so that Allah's plan may reach its completion, the deeds of people may be recompensed with reward and punishment, and man may be held accountable for the path he chooses for himself and be rewarded or punished accordingly.

"Liyu'adhdhiba Allahu al-munafiqina ... wa kana Allahu ghafuran rahiman" (33:73): "So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and women, and the polytheist men and women, and accept the repentance of the believing men and women. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Lesson No. 193: Explanation of the Verses

63 ... to ... 73

"Yas'aluka an-nasu 'ani as-sa'ati ... takuna qariban" (33:63): The people of Makkah kept asking the Messenger of Allah about the Day of Resurrection, because the Prophet (ﷺ) had described to them the conditions of the Hour in great detail and had warned them of it very strongly. The Qur'an had described the scenes of the Resurrection at such length that it seemed as though these scenes were before their eyes. O Prophet, these people ask you about the time of the occurrence of the Hour. Their desire is that it come quickly, and they were hastening because in reality they doubted its occurrence. Or, by demanding haste, they actually wanted to deny it, or wanted to make a jest of the Hour. Every questioner's question was according to his psychology, and according to his thoughts and his beliefs he would ask in accordance with his conviction.

Knowledge of the Hour is an unseen matter that is exclusive to Allah, and Allah has not informed any of His creatures of it, neither the Messengers nor the nearest angels. In the hadith about the reality of faith and the reality of Islam narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar, it is related that we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when suddenly a man appeared, wearing completely white clothing. There was no trace of travel upon him, and none of us recognised him. He sat down before the Messenger of Allah, placed his knees against the knees of the Messenger of Allah, put his hands upon his thighs, and said: "O Muhammad, tell me what Islam is." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Islam is that you bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer, pay the zakat, fast in Ramadan, and perform the Hajj if you have the means." He said: "You have spoken truly." We were amazed that he asked and then himself confirmed the answer. Then he asked: "Tell me what faith is." The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that you believe in good and evil decree." He said: "You have spoken rightly." Then he asked: "Tell me what excellence (ihsan) is." The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "That you worship your Lord as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you." Then he asked: "Tell me about the Hour." The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "The one asked knows no more than the one asking." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That was Jibril (Gabriel) (peace be upon him); he came to you teaching you your religion."

The one about whom the question was asked was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the questioner was Jibril. The knowledge of both was equal, that is, both did not know about the Hour.

"Qul innama 'ilmuha 'inda Allah" (33:63): "Say: its knowledge is only with Allah." This is a specific attribute of Allah, and Allah alone is singular in it, and none of Allah's creation has knowledge of it.

It is the wisdom of Allah that He has not given knowledge of it to anyone. As far as our understanding goes, the wisdom is that people should always fear it, always anticipate it, and remain engaged in preparing for its sudden arrival. This applies to those whom Allah has turned towards the path of goodness through it, and has placed in their hearts the fear of the Hour. As for those who are heedless of it and do not remain constantly engaged in preparing for it, they betray themselves and do not protect themselves from the Fire. For such people, Allah has set before them its scenes, warned them of it, and described it as an unseen matter that can come at any time, day or night.

"Wa ma yudrika la'alla as-sa'ata takunu qariban" (33:63): "And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 64–68:

ان اللہ لعن الکفرین ۔۔۔۔۔۔ من العذاب والعنھم لعنا کبیرا (64 – 68) ”

These people ask about the Establishment of the Hour; just describe to them a scene of the Hour.

إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا (33:64) "Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire." Allah has removed the disbelievers far from His mercy, and has prepared for them a blazing Fire. It is ready and present for them.

خالدين فيها (33:65) "Abiding therein forever." They will remain in it for a period so long that only Allah knows its extent. It has no end, except what is within Allah's knowledge; when He wills, He will end it. No one will assist them, and no helper will be available. Therefore, they will have no hope of escaping from this Fire.

لا يجدون ولياً ولا نصيراً (33:65) "They will not find any protector or helper." What will be their condition in this punishment? An extremely wretched state and a most painful situation:

يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار (33:66) "On the Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire." Fire will envelop them from every side. Here the image of their movements is being filmed, as it were, and presented in embodied form, such that every part of their faces will be scorched by the Fire, and thus they will be given the most severe torment.

يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا (33:66) "They will say, 'Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!'" This will be a wholly futile wish on their part, for then where will be the occasion for obedience? At that time there will be no opportunity for trial. Now there is only regret. Now they will become furious with their leaders and elders, who in truth led them astray, and they will strive to become obedient to Allah, but the opportunity for obedience will have passed.

وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ والعنهم لعنا كبيرا (33:67–68) "And they will say, 'Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us away from the right path. Our Lord, give them double punishment and curse them with a great curse.'" This is the sample of the Hour. What are you asking about? On that Day, the only way to be saved is to prepare for it, otherwise this dreadful end will be before you.

When the marriage of Zaynab with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went against a deeply rooted custom of the Jahiliyyah, and Islam had struck a decisive blow against it through the action of the Messenger ﷺ, that society did not accept the uprooting of this custom from within itself without feeling pain. The hypocrites and people of diseased character began a fierce uproar. Those Muslims whose understanding of the Islamic concept of life had not yet firmly settled into their minds would agree with them. Accordingly, these elements engaged in taunts, objections and criticism. Throughout the city they began whispering, and they spoke evil things about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

How could the hypocrites and the spreaders of rumours remain silent? They would not let any occasion slip from their hands, just as in the Battle of the Confederates they had launched a massive campaign. ... They had already tested themselves in the matter of ... Previously they had run a similar campaign in the distribution of the spoils of war. In short, in every circumstance these people were a source of torment to the Prophet ﷺ, and that without any justification.

In this period, when Banu Qurayzah and all the Jews had been expelled from Madinah, there was no disbeliever or polytheist in Madinah. The people of Madinah were either true Muslims or hypocrites, and this kind of campaign was run by none other than these hypocrites. They spread false rumours. Some simple-minded Muslims were also influenced by them, and joined them out of lack of understanding. Therefore, the Holy Qur'an here warns the believers: do not become a source of torment to the Prophet ﷺ. Earlier, the believing companions of Musa (peace be upon him) had also tormented Musa. Therefore, do not lend an ear to the words of these hypocrites without verification and investigation. Obey Allah and His Messenger; this will be a great success for you.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verses 69–71:**

﴿Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu la takunu﴾ ....... ﴿fa-faza fawzan ʿaẓīma﴾ (69–71)

The Qur'an does not specify the harm that was inflicted on Prophet Musa (Moses). However, the narrations do specify it. Therefore, we leave this matter unspecified, as the Qur'an has left it unspecified. The purpose here is to warn the believers not to cause harm to the Holy Prophet (ﷺ). In the Qur'an, Allah has given many examples of the misdeeds and wicked conduct of the Children of Israel. Here, Allah has pointed out that they had harmed their Prophet. Therefore, Muslims should not do such things, so that the consciousness of Muslims becomes such that they do not resemble the Children of Israel in any matter. Hatred of them should settle in their hearts, because these people were embodiments of evil conduct and deviation, and were constantly troubling their Prophet.

Allah had cleared the Prophet of the accusation that the Children of Israel had made against him.

﴿wa kana ʿinda Allahi wajihan﴾ (33:69) "And he was honorable in the sight of Allah." That is, he was one of dignity and high standing with Allah. It is the sunnah (divine way and practice) of Allah that He clears His Messengers of every kind of slander and accusation, completely and perfectly, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is superior to all the Prophets; therefore, Allah clears and purifies him as well.

The Qur'an guides the believers that, in any matter, before agreeing with the hypocrites and enemies, it is obligatory to investigate and verify its accuracy. Especially concerning their Prophet, their guide, their protector and their friend, they should refrain from paying attention to the words of the misguided and the wicked and sinful. The Qur'an guides them to a righteous word, from which righteous action emerges. Allah watches over those who are truthful and guides them towards good deeds. Allah forgives those who speak good words and do good deeds, and pardons their shortcomings, because no person is free from shortcomings. A person can be freed from these shortcomings only through the forgiveness of Allah.

﴿man yuṭiʿi Allaha wa rasulahu faqad faza fawzan ʿaẓīman﴾ (33:71) "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment." Obedience to Allah is itself a great success, because through obedience a person is established upon the way of Allah. Steadfastness on the path of Allah is beneficial for a person. And the one who has been guided to the straight path and the way of Allah, this itself is lasting felicity and good fortune, even if there is no other reward or recompense for him beyond it. For the one who is rightly progressing towards his destination, who sees his path clearly, and around whom all creation is supportive, cannot be like the one who does not know his way, is confused, and for whom the whole universe on his path is in conflict and is painful. Therefore, obedience to Allah and His Messenger is itself the best recompense. This is the great success. It is a success even before the Day of Reckoning and the blissful Paradise. The success in the Hereafter is a great grace, and it is a bonus; the blessing that will be given, and this grace, Allah gives to whomever He wills. This grace of Allah is because the human being is very weak. The responsibility that Allah has placed upon human shoulders is very heavy, and man, out of his ignorance, has taken upon himself such a great burden that the heavens, the earth and the mountains refused to bear it. Yet he knew his own weaknesses: the pressure of desires and inclinations, the deficiency of knowledge and skill, the brevity of life, the difficulties of time and place, and human weakness in foreseeing future events, and so on.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 72:

إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا الْأَمَانَةَ ... ظَلُومًا جَهُولًا (72)

Indeed, We offered the trust (al-amanah) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were afraid of it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.

The great beings of the heavens and the earth, and the mountains within the earth, which the Qur'an mentions here, are in truth vast creations for the ordinary human being, and within them man lives; in comparison with them, man is very weak and insignificant. These creations know their Creator well and move according to Allah's cosmic system and law. They directly receive Allah's commands and act upon them. They proceed according to the natural order (namus al-fitrah) which Allah has set within them. From the beginning of creation, the universe has continued in this way, according to the system of qada' and qadar. It does not step out of Allah's obedience, nor does it deviate from His natural order even by a hair's breadth, nor is it able to do so. All these creations are performing their appointed duties, whether or not they have awareness, and whether or not they have any choice.

This sun revolves in its orbit, and there is no disturbance in its course. It shines, and so long as Allah commands, it continues to warm and illuminate the universe. Then the family of this sun also performs its duties precisely within its sphere, carrying out its appointed functions.

This earth revolves in its orbit. As a result of this rotation, crops grow, the provision for human beings is arranged, it gathers the dead, springs of water burst forth from within it, and all of this happens according to the Sunnah of Allah, without any intention on the part of the earth.

These moon, stars and planets, these winds and clouds, or this water and this sea, these mountains and these plains, all of them carry out their respective duties by the command of their Lord and by the decree of their Creator, and all these things perform their duties without toil or exertion. These pillars of the universe could not bear it; they were frightened and terrified. They were unable to bear this great trust. What was this trust? It was to carry out one's duties by one's own will and choice, and to be responsible for one's deeds and actions. But!

وَحَمَلَهَا الْإِنْسَانُ (33:72) "But man took it up." Man, who knows Allah through his consciousness and his perception, who through his reflection and insight discerns the natural order, and who through his striving and effort lives according to that order, obeys Allah by his own will and takes up responsibilities deliberately. He controls his inclinations and desires. At every step of his life he acts with conscious will. He has awareness of his path, deliberately chooses his way for himself, and walks upon the path of another with understanding and insight.

This is the great trust which this human being took up, although man was very weak, feeble, small and powerless. Just as his strength was limited, so was his lifespan limited, and then upon this weak human being, from every side, armies of inclinations, desires and natural appetites were attacking.

From this standpoint, this weak human being took upon his shoulders a great responsibility. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. He wronged his own self by placing this heavy burden upon himself, and he was unaware of his lack of strength. But when a human being fulfils the responsibility he has taken up, and when he reaches the Almighty through his recognition and his perception, then he directly attains the knowledge of Allah's natural order and becomes fully obedient to the will of his Lord. This recognition, this guidance and this obedience reach a lofty station in their reality and in their effects, and they operate in such a self-acting manner as the heavens, the earth and the mountains readily and directly submit to guidance, recognition and obedience, because all these creations directly possess the knowledge of Allah. They proceed directly under Allah's guidance, they obey directly, and there is no barrier or obstacle between them and the Almighty, and nothing prevents them from obeying Allah. So when man too, like this entire universe, becomes bound to Allah's recognition, guidance and obedience, then at that time he becomes one who has reached Allah (wasil billah), and

Then his station among Allah's creatures becomes unique.

The truth is that will, perception, choice and the bearing of responsibility are the distinguishing characteristics of man, and by virtue of them man holds an exalted position among these creatures. This is the honour and dignity which Allah proclaimed in the higher realm, when He commanded the angels to prostrate before this human being, and He inscribed this proclamation in the Qur'an until the Day of Resurrection.

وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي آدَمَ "Indeed, We have honoured the children of Adam." Man should understand the true reason for this honour, and should discharge well the trust which Allah has placed in his care, which he has accepted, and at whose bearing the heavens, the earth and the mountains refused and were frightened. This trust or responsibility: why did Allah place it upon man?

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 33, verse 73:**

﴿Liyu'adhdhiba Allahu al-munafiqina ... ghafuran rahiman﴾ (73)

What are the qualities that man has taken upon his shoulders? That he should recognize himself, attain knowledge of his conduct through his rational faculty, act by his own will, and reach God himself. Thus he should make correct use of his choice and be responsible for the recompense and punishment of his deeds. In this way, the hypocrite men and hypocrite women become deserving of punishment, the polytheist men and polytheist women reach their end, and God helps the believing men and believing women and forgives the shortcomings, weaknesses and frailties that proceed from them. For in the path of man there are countless obstacles: weakness, frailty, desires, emotions, inclinations and the influences of society, and he has the greatest need of the mercy and forgiveness of God, and God is indeed Ghafur and Rahim.

With this magnificent commentary and this final and forceful blow upon the strings of reason and understanding, the surah concludes. It began with the theme that O Prophet, you should obey God and not follow the desires of the disbelievers and hypocrites. Act in accordance with God's revelation and indications, rely upon God, and do not depend upon any power other than God. After this, the legislation necessary for the Islamic system of life and practical guidance for the Islamic state were given, with the command to follow God's law and God's wisdom in strategy.

In this final blow and commentary it is shown that one should feel, even slightly, the responsibility that is placed upon man. How great was this responsibility? That the mountains trembled at its bearing. The summary of this is that just as this universe is obedient to the order of God, man should, by willing submission, attain access to the order of God and become obedient, and obey the will of God.

The surah ends with this commentary. Its beginning and its end are mutually proportionate, and the whole surah moves in the direction of this beginning and end, in perfect harmony. From this it becomes clear that the same Gracious Being who sent this Book is the One who sustains this universe.
